text:
Pulling Talarico’s clip and the Western record on speech, migration, culture, and state-managed death so the rewrite matches the charge's size. His mother’s courage is not on trial. A woman walked out of a violent house, took a hotel job, found a cheap apartment in East Austin, and looked for a party that would not leave her on the floor. That happened. It does not decide what the word Democrat means in 2026, and it does not decide what the left is doing to every country that still lets it run the schools, the clinics, the border, and the microphone.

https://t.co/43kk5OAueb

James Talarico told Joe Rogan he is a Democrat because Democrats fight for the little guy, and because Ann Richards looked like that fight to his mother. Fine, as a child. A party is not a lullaby. A party is what it does after it has the offices. The left that now owns that word — in Texas, in London, in Ottawa, in Brussels, in Canberra — is not Ann Richards with better lighting. It is one machine with local nameplates.

Look at the West and try to find the exception.

Britain arrests people by the tens of thousands for words. Big Brother Watch and the Free Speech Union report more than 62,000 arrests for communications offenses in five years — on the order of thirty to forty people a day — while ordinary street crime goes unsolved. A man can be pulled in for a meme about Hamas. The same state lectures you about kindness.

https://t.co/aj3I2XMCtw

Canada built a death service and called it medicine. They sold medical assistance in dying as a rare mercy for the dying. It became a system that has already taken tens of thousands of lives. Poverty, isolation, and “feeling like a burden” show up in the testimony. Parliament is still wrestling with whether to open it to mental illness as the sole condition in 2027. A country that will help you die faster than it will house you or treat you has told you what the little guy is worth.

https://t.co/lr54hElrYm

The same pattern walks through the Netherlands and Belgium, through “assisted dying” bills in Britain and Australia, through American campuses and clinics that treat a healthy body as raw material for a fashion. That is not thirty separate accidents. That is a class that has decided some lives are inventory.

Migration is not a mystery either. The same parties, the same NGOs, the same UN language, the same sermons about “compassion,” opened the door and then punished the native who noticed the street change. They imported a political religion that does not share their speech rules, their women, or their churches, and then called the notice racism. When jihad shows its face, they hunt the meme harder than the cell. You asked for a Western liberal country where that is not the fight. Name it. The pause is the answer.

Culture is next. Tear down the statue, rewrite the founding as a crime scene, tell the children their parents are the stain, put a boy in a girl’s locker room and call the father a bigot. Hamilton in Kansas said his own suburb was too beige. That is the same sermon Talarico’s party sings with better manners. A people that must become less itself to deserve its young is a people being prepared for administration.

Enslavement here is not a chain on the ankle. It is a life that cannot speak, cannot keep a neighborhood, cannot afford the first room, cannot get a doctor who is not a salesman, and is offered a needle when the math of care gets expensive. The little guy becomes a client. Clients do not fire the ministry. They wait for the next benefit and hope the speech law does not notice their mouth.

Gøtzsche already said the quiet part about the drug industry: a business model that matches organized crime, pills that kill people who never needed them, a party that sat in the waiting room and took the check.

https://t.co/ikVc7BK2eF

This has nothing to do with a church. A church names sin and keeps a child. This machine empties the church, then fills the vacancy with pride flags, climate liturgy, and a hatred of limits. Nihilism is the solvent. If nothing is holy, a commission can replace a people, a doctor can end a poor man, and a pastor-in-training can still say “little guy” while the coalition that pays him needs the little guy dependent, silent, and grateful.

Is there a smoke-filled room with one satanic letterhead? You do not need the letterhead. You need the product: the same speech code, the same migration theology, the same sex-and-child experiments, the same apology for the nation’s dead, the same offer of death when the person cannot pull weight. Foundations, treaty language, universities, and parties move in time. That is coordination enough. Call it Davos, the UN, the donor class, or a nihilvultarch high command. The fruit is the same.

Talarico is fluent and sincere. Sincerity is how the machine borrows a mother’s story. She left a man who hurt her because she would not live inside someone else’s appetite. The honest update is this: the party that wears her memory now stays, explains, imports the danger, polices the sentence, and sends a bill. If Democrats still fight for the people, show the cities they have held for fifty years and point to the people who got stronger. If the people got smaller while the donors got a ministry, the name on the card is not a lineage. It is a habit.

Love your mother. Keep her courage. Stop confusing a 1990s story with a 2026 occupation. Judge the occupation by the apartment, the school, the street, the mouth that may not speak, and the clinic that learned to kill. If the little guy is still the point, the little guy gets to fire the brand that failed him. That is not hate. That is the same decision she already made.

text:
Rep. Nancy Mace, a Republican from South Carolina, has introduced a bill to end the breeding of dogs for medical research. Under the PUPPS Act, companies could no longer breed or sell dogs to laboratories, and labs could not knowingly buy them. Violators would lose their federal license and face fines of up to $10,000 per dog, or $40,000 for repeat offenses. Dogs already in labs would be offered for adoption instead of being put down. "Dogs aren't lab equipment. They're family," Mace wrote.
 
The bill follows records obtained by White Coat Waste, a group that campaigns against taxpayer-funded animal testing. According to the group, a single Illinois breeder, Oak Hill Genetics, sold 1,518 dogs to 44 labs between January 2025 and June 2026, including universities that used them in heart, stroke and cancer studies.
 
More than 40,000 dogs were used in U.S. research in the 2024 fiscal year, USDA figures show. A 2020 National Academies review of dog research at the Department of Veterans Affairs found dogs were still scientifically necessary in only a few areas, such as heart rhythm studies and devices that help people with spinal cord injuries breathe.
 
Mace introduced the bill on Sept. 21, and it has no cosponsors yet. She leaves Congress in January after losing the Republican primary for South Carolina governor in June, and any bill that has not passed by then expires.
 
——
Let’s hope this passes. Thank you @NancyMace @RepNancyMace

text:
I opened the bedroom door and immediately wished I could unsee what was lying beside my roommate’s sleeping face.

I’m 28, and I share a townhouse in Manchester with my roommate, Caleb. My girlfriend, Nora, works late shifts, and Caleb had offered to pick her up from work that evening since he was already going to be awake.

The arrangement seemed completely normal.

Caleb works nights, so his sleep schedule is strange. He usually asks me to wake him if he accidentally falls asleep because otherwise he’ll sleep through the time he’s supposed to leave.

That night, I walked past his room and noticed he had fallen asleep.

I was about to quietly wake him when something caught my attention.

A pair of my underwear was lying on the floor right beside his face.

I froze.

My first thought was that there had to be a completely innocent explanation. Maybe I’d accidentally left it there. Maybe it had gotten mixed in with laundry.

But the closer I looked, the more uncomfortable I became.

Why was it there?

Why hadn’t he moved it?

And why did my heart suddenly feel like it was trying to escape my chest?

I took a quick photo because I knew I would probably question my own memory later.

Then I walked away.

I felt sick.

I didn’t know what had happened, but I knew I couldn’t pretend I hadn’t seen it.

text:
Five brothers are lost and thirsty. At a well they find a hideous old woman who will give water only to whoever kisses her. Four of them refuse. The fifth becomes High King of Ireland. 👑 The hag at the well.
This is one of the central stories of Irish kingship, and it explains an idea that runs underneath a great deal of the mythology. The five sons of Eochaid Mugmedón are out hunting and become lost, and they grow desperate for water. One by one they come upon a well, and guarding it is an old woman of appalling ugliness, described in the texts in unsparing detail, black as coal, with teeth like a hedge and green nails. She tells each of them that they may drink only if they give her a kiss. Four of the brothers refuse outright, or offer the barest peck and are sent away with nothing. Then Niall comes. He not only kisses her, he embraces her fully and without reluctance. And as he does, she transforms in his arms into the most beautiful woman in the world. He asks who she is, and she gives the answer the whole story exists for. I am Sovereignty, she says, Flaithius, the kingship of Ireland, and as you have seen me, so is the kingship. Ugly and harsh at the first, and beautiful in the end. She grants him the kingship, and tells him it will remain with his descendants, and Niall becomes Niall of the Nine Hostages, ancestor of the Uí Néill dynasty that dominated Ireland for centuries. The idea underneath it is the oldest in Irish political thought. Kingship is not something a man takes by force. It is a marriage with the land itself, personified as a woman, and the land grants it to the one who is willing to accept it as it actually is, hardship and all. A false or unjust king caused the land to fail, and a true king brought good harvests, because the relationship was real. The same loathly lady turns up later in Arthurian literature and in Chaucer, and the Irish versions are among the earliest.
He embraced her as she was, and she was the country. 💚 A central story of Irish kingship, the hag at the well who demands a kiss and transforms into a beautiful woman revealing herself as Sovereignty, granting the kingship to Niall because he accepted the land as it actually was.

text:
The Evolution of the Guitar Tremolo - Inventors and Evolution 1920s-2026

The guitar “tremolo” is technically a vibrato system - it changes pitch by altering string tension rather than changing volume. Its evolution spans nearly a century of attempts to increase pitch range while improving tuning stability and feel.

Clayton “Doc” Kauffman pioneered one of the earliest commercially important systems with his Vib-Rola in the 1920s-30s. Its spring-loaded mechanism changed string tension mechanically, establishing a principle followed by virtually every later design.

Paul Bigsby transformed that idea into a durable professional system around 1951. His cast-aluminum vibrato used a rotating string bar working against a compression spring. Adopted by Gretsch, Gibson and others, the Bigsby became the first widely successful vibrato tailpiece.

Under Ted McCarty, Gibson developed its own systems. The unusual sideways Vibrola appeared around 1961, followed by simpler Maestro Vibrolas associated particularly with SGs and Firebirds.

Leo Fender fundamentally changed the design in 1954. The Stratocaster’s synchronized tremolo combined bridge and tailpiece into a pivoting assembly balanced between string tension and rear-mounted springs. Individual adjustable saddles made the system remarkably versatile and established the architecture from which many modern tremolos descend.

Fender took another route with the 1958 Jazzmaster. Its floating tremolo separated the spring-loaded tailpiece from a rocking bridge, with the Jaguar adopting the system in 1962.

Floyd D. Rose addressed the persistent problem of strings slipping at the nut and bridge during the 1970s. His double-locking system clamped the strings at both ends and incorporated fine tuners. By the early 1980s, it allowed radical dives and pull-ups while maintaining substantially greater tuning stability.

Kahler offered a different solution in the early 1980s. Dave Storey’s cam-operated design used individual roller saddles and a rotating cam rather than a conventional pivoting bridge plate.

Paul Reed Smith refined the synchronized concept during the 1980s with a precisely engineered six-pivot bridge integrated with the nut, tuners and string path as a complete system.

Modern two-point tremolos further simplified Fender’s concept by replacing six pivot screws with two posts and knife-edge pivots. Better machining, low-friction nuts, locking tuners and improved saddles have progressively reduced friction and tuning problems.

The goal: move six strings through substantial pitch changes and return every one of them accurately to pitch.

America’s Mayor Tells Lara Logan He Knew by Nightfall on January 6 That It Was a “Fixed Operation” — And He Names the Man He Says Owns the Darkest Hours in American History 
America’s Mayor just said the quiet part out loud.

Former New York City Mayor and Trump attorney Rudy Giuliani dropped a series of explosive allegations Saturday night during the American Martyrs premiere in West Palm Beach, Florida, telling moderator Lara Logan that by the time he went to bed on January 6, 2021, he believed he knew exactly what had happened.

Giuliani said he did not need Liz Cheney’s television committee, an Obama-era prosecutor, or four years of cable-news sermons to understand January 6.

“It was a very unusual experience for me because, let me begin by telling you, by the time I went to sleep on the evening of January 6th, I knew exactly what was going on,” Giuliani told Logan. “I knew exactly that it was a fixed operation.”

Logan pressed him on the security failures that left the Capitol wide open, the same failures The Gateway Pundit has documented for years while the corporate press screamed “insurrection” and ignored the stand-down.

She told Giuliani she called his former NYPD police commissioner, Bernard Kerik — the 9/11-era commissioner who later worked the 2020 election files with Giuliani — and asked him a simple law-enforcement question, stripped of politics:

If you wanted to secure the Capitol that day, what would you have done?

Kerik’s answer, Logan said, was immediate: put mounted officers around the building. Circle the Capitol on horseback. One mounted officer, Kerik told her, is worth about three men on the ground.

They didn’t do that.

They didn’t do a lot of things a serious police department would have done.

As Fox News reported, leaked footage filmed by Nancy Pelosi’s own daughter captured the then-Speaker admitting, “I take responsibility,” after security collapsed — and the White House later documented Pelosi’s refusal of the 10,000 National Guard troops President Trump offered in advance.

Former Capitol Police Chief Steven Sund has said he made 11 urgent calls for the Guard starting at 12:58 p.m. and waited 71 minutes for approval from the House Sergeant at Arms, who reported to Pelosi.

Optics over officers. Politics over the perimeter.

That is not a riot that “just happened.” That is a building left unsecured on purpose.

“The Guy Responsible for the Darkest Hours in American History Is Barack Obama”
Logan asked Giuliani what he saw as the indicators that January 6 was an operation.

Giuliani did not hedge.

He said he now agrees “completely with General Flynn” that the man responsible for “the darkest hours in American history is Barack Obama.”

“You know how they talk about an Antichrist? He’s an anti-president,” Giuliani said. “And I believe now all the things that I thought were exaggerated way back then, I believe he was flagrant.”

Giuliani said, “As part of the communist plan… to overthrow us.”

Trump Wasn’t There to “Incite a Riot.” He Was There Because Pence Wouldn’t Do His Job.
Giuliani reminded Logan what he was actually doing that week.

He was still Trump’s impeachment lawyer. He was still trying to get Vice President Mike Pence to pause the count. Four state legislatures had written Pence asking him to wait. Giuliani said two of those packets — Georgia and Pennsylvania — were “ironclad.” Arizona was “very, very cozy.” Wisconsin, he said, was “a completely illegal election.”

On Wisconsin, Giuliani walked through the absentee-affidavit rule the state’s own law imposed: no affidavit, the vote is canceled. “If you canceled all the votes that didn’t have an affidavit, Trump would have won,” he said. The Wisconsin Supreme Court called the penalty “too harsh.” Giuliani’s word for that ruling: “absurd.”

On Pennsylvania, he said the state Supreme Court signed off on roughly 900,000 ballots counted without a Republican inspector able to actually observe the count — because one Republican sitting in a room “the size of a basketball arena” was treated as if he could see a count happening on the other side of the floor.

“One judge, the Republican, voted and said, you’re really reducing him to a potted plant,” Giuliani said. “And it’s an absurd decision.”

That is the context the fake-news networks never give you when they clip “trial by combat” and run it on a loop.

Giuliani said he was not even supposed to speak at the Ellipse rally. He was working the legislatures. The majority leader of the Pennsylvania legislature, he said, started out hostile — stuck Giuliani’s first hearing in the suburbs so “nobody would hear us” — then called him after seeing the evidence.

“This is an outrage,” Giuliani recalled the lawmaker saying. “They stole a million votes.”

“I know. What are you going to do about it?”

“I’m going to write a letter.”

He wrote it. Pence ignored it.

“Pence. The terrible vice president,” Giuliani said. “Pence just disregarded it.”

That morning, Giuliani said, White House Chief of Staff Mark Meadows called.

President Trump wanted constitutional scholar John Eastman to explain that alternate electors were not some invented coup — they had been used before, including in the 1960 Kennedy-Nixon contest, and flow from a reading of the Constitution “accepted by all the liberal jackass professors at Harvard.”

The problem, Meadows told him: Eastman “doesn’t speak English, he speaks lawyer.” The president wanted Giuliani standing there to interpret.

Giuliani and Eastman went early. They froze on the stage for hours. “Thought we were gonna die of pneumonia like one of those presidents did,” Giuliani said.

Then he gave the line the regime spent years trying to turn into a crime.

“Why don’t we have the machines? I’ll take the machine that I analyzed, you take your machine, Dominion. Let’s have a trial by combat.”

Congress sued him for inciting a riot.

“Believe it or not,” Giuliani said, “an Obama judge dismissed the case against me, saying it was ridiculous.”

He went home, locked down at his compound, and kept working the states with Kerik’s investigative team — six states, still trying to get Pence to give them the kind of delay Thomas Jefferson once used.

Pence never did.

This Is the Story the J6 Committee Was Built to Bury
None of this is new to Gateway Pundit readers. It is new only to people who still get their news from the people who ran the cover-up.

As TGP previously reported, Giuliani asked the questions Pelosi’s committee refused to touch:

Why did Speaker Pelosi refuse the National Guard President Trump offered?
Why were Capitol officers seen opening doors?
What role did the FBI and Antifa play?
Why did the committee pretend officers were “killed by the mob” when no officer was killed in the way they sold it?
Why did they ignore the killing of unarmed Air Force veteran Ashli Babbitt?

text:
Good morning from Virginia 🇺🇸

On this day in 1780, George Washington sat fourteen of his generals down at Tappan, New York, and asked them a question that would stain the Revolution with both justice and regret.

Major John André, Adjutant General of the British Army, stood before them. Handsome, educated, composed. The man who had just been caught with Benedict Arnold’s plot to sell West Point stuffed in his boots.

This was no ordinary court. Nathanael Greene sat as president. Around him were Lafayette, Baron von Steuben, Henry Knox, Lord Stirling, Arthur St. Clair, Robert Howe, and a line of brigadiers who had already bled for the cause—Parsons, Clinton, Glover, Paterson, Hand, Huntington, Stark. Judge Advocate John Laurance ran the examination. Alexander Hamilton was not on that board. He was Washington’s aide, close enough to watch the whole tragedy unfold, and later close enough to admit how much the prisoner had moved him.

The facts were merciless.

André had come ashore from HMS Vulture in the night to meet Arnold. When the ship was driven downriver, he was stranded behind American lines. He put on civilian clothes. He took the name John Anderson. He accepted Arnold’s pass under that false name. He hid maps, strength reports, and the keys to West Point against his skin and started walking toward New York.

Under the law of nations, that made him a spy.

André did not crawl. He did not blame Arnold to save his neck. He told the board, with almost reckless honesty, that he had not come ashore under a flag of truce. That single admission cut the last rope his friends in New York were trying to throw him. Clinton and Arnold both claimed otherwise in letters. André, who had not seen those letters, contradicted them to his own face.

The board was unanimous. He “ought to be considered as a Spy from the Enemy,” and “agreeable to the Law and usage of Nations” he ought to suffer death.

Then came the part that still sits uneasy in American memory.

The same officers who condemned him admired him. Lafayette wrote that the court was filled with admiration and compassion. Steuben growled that André had put them to no proof—he confessed everything except a planned desire to deceive—and wished the wretch who had drawn him into it could have hung in his place. Washington himself offered the British a trade that every man in camp understood: André’s life for Arnold’s body. Sir Henry Clinton refused. A defector returned would poison every future desertion. British honor, such as it was that week, would not stretch that far.

André asked for a gentleman’s death—the firing squad. Washington denied it. Spies were hanged. The law had to look the same for a charming major as for a common thief, or it was not law.

Three days later, on October 2, they walked him to the gallows at Tappan. He tied his own handkerchief, thanked the officers who had treated him well, and died with the composure that had already won half the Continental Army.

Arnold slept that night under a British roof.

That is the hard edge of 1780. Treason can wear a general’s star and still slip the noose. The man who kept his word, told the truth, and refused to crawl paid the price the rules demanded.

Remember both names. One is a warning. The other is a reminder that even in a war for liberty, the law does not blink because the prisoner has manners.

Nice conspiracy theory.  

Stalin's wariness of British infiltration into Soviet Central Asia via Xinjiang was a core driver of Soviet policy in the region from the 1930s to 1945 as China was mired in civil and war with Japanese Imperial Army and the different regions were run by warlords. Stalin’s interest was rooted in a profound sense of vulnerability regarding the USSR's vast, resource-rich, and potentially restive Central Asian territories that abut Chinese Xinjiang. The fear was not of a conventional British military invasion, but of a more insidious form of subversion: the use of Xinjiang as a base for intelligence gathering, the fomenting of anti-Soviet rebellions among Muslim populations, and the broader geopolitical encirclement of the Soviet Union.

Any Soviet interest in Aksai Chin in the 1930 to 1945 was because Aksai Chin was historically an uninhabited, high-altitude desert (terra incognita), but it offered one key geographical asset: flat, high-altitude terrain linking Xinjiang to Western Tibet. After 1949 when Mao declared the setting up of the PRC after winning the civil war against the KMT, Stalin stop all secret activities in China as it wanted to support the PRC under Mao. China built the 219/G219 highway from 1951 to 1957 (6 years) in broad daylight and after completion – in 1958 suddenly it was informed by India that Aksai Chin was India’s territory as India finally realized that a long highway has been built on their “land” over a 6-year period by Chinese engineers in broad daylight without their discovering it! As the British map in the 19th Century was not clear about Aksai Chin, Nehru started to issue new map to include Aksai Chin into Independent India’s territory as a precaution.

To give some background:

The British Presence in Xinjiang: A "Listening Post" on the Soviet Frontier

The primary instrument of British activity in the region was its Consulate-General in Kashgar, the only official British diplomatic post in Xinjiang. This consulate was not merely a commercial or diplomatic office; it functioned as a crucial intelligence-gathering hub focused on the Soviet Union's southern frontier.

British intelligence officers in Kashgar, such as Clarmont Skrine and P. T. Etherton, were deeply involved in monitoring Soviet activities, communications, and the political pulse of Soviet Central Asia. From this vantage point, they could observe Soviet troop movements, economic developments, and any signs of unrest. For Stalin, this British "listening post" represented a direct and continuous threat to the secrecy and security of his most vulnerable border region.

Fomenting Rebellion: The Threat from Within

Beyond mere observation, the Soviets believed the British were actively working to destabilize their Central Asian republics by exploiting ethnic and religious tensions. The Soviet security apparatus (NKVD) uncovered evidence of British intelligence organizing and inspiring uprisings in Xinjiang against governments friendly to the USSR.

A key figure in these Soviet narratives was Akmal Ikramov, a Soviet official who was accused of being a British agent. According to interrogation records, in 1935-1936, on behalf of British intelligence, Ikramov organized meetings with local leaders to "discuss the preparation of uprisings in Xinjiang". The aim was to spread British influence in the region and, by extension, create a zone of instability on the Soviet Union's doorstep.

This fear was part of a broader Soviet belief in a "Second Tournament of Shadows"—a continuation of the 19th-century Great Game—where Britain, and later Germany, were seen as actively collaborating to use Central Asian territories, including Xinjiang, as a platform for anti-Soviet activities.

In 1936 Japan & Germany signed an Anti-Comintern Pact to jointly oppose Communist International (Comintern) arm of the USSR, that was actively exporting Soviet style of Communism to developing countries.  A Chinese Politburo document frames the intervention as a direct response to "the intrigues of Japanese imperialism in Xinjiang" portraying Hui Muslim warlord Ma Zhongying and other rivals as "Japanese agents".

The Geopolitical Imperative: Securing the "Soft Underbelly"

Stalin's concern was strategic and deeply personal. The Soviet Central Asian republics were a "soft underbelly"—vast, resource-rich, and historically connected to the wider Islamic and Asian world. The fear was that British subversion could spark a Pan-Islamic or nationalist movement that would threaten Soviet control over the region.

This threat was amplified by the belief that Britain was coordinating its efforts with Japan, which was expanding its influence from Manchuria. The specter of a coordinated Anglo-Japanese pincer movement against the USSR, with Xinjiang as a key corridor, was a central Soviet anxiety. British intelligence reports from the time even noted a rumor that Hitler was urging the Russians to act against British interests in Xinjiang, highlighting the complex web of perceived threats.

Stalin made his fears explicit during his meeting with its proxy - the Xinjiang warlord Sheng Shicai in Moscow in August 1938. He warned Sheng to be constantly alert to "infiltration by Japanese Fascist spies as well as British Imperialist spies". This was a direct, personal articulation of the Soviet leader's belief that Xinjiang was a battleground for foreign espionage and subversion.

Conclusion: A Strategic Obsession

For Stalin, British activities in Xinjiang were not a peripheral concern but a direct threat to the territorial integrity of the USSR. The fear of British or Japanese infiltration was a key factor driving the Soviet decision to militarily support Sheng Shicai in the 1930s, as a way to secure a compliant buffer state and deny a base of operations to its rivals. By propping up warlord Sheng and later supporting the Ili Rebellion, Stalin was ultimately able to isolate Xinjiang from non-Soviet influence and protect the "soft underbelly" of his empire. This strategic imperative remained constant from the 1930s through the end of World War II. When Mao won the civil war and the PRC was formed, the secret activity in Xinjiang stopped.

text:
India's oldest brand has no price tag

If you want to understand the Guru, stop reading business papers. Sit at your grandmother's pooja on Guru Purnima and watch her bow. She isn't a customer and nobody has sold her anything. She is bowing to something that was here long before IIM, Shark Tank or D2C.
Welcome to India's oldest institution: the Guru parampara.
We like to think anything that grows fast must be a business. That's a very new-age idea. The parampara is older than money. It started with Adiyogi, the first Guru, who sat by Kanti Sarovar and gave the science of yoga to seven disciples, the Saptarishis. There was no fee, no funnel and no WhatsApp forward. For thousands of years, that transmission has passed from Guru to disciple, from Kashi to Kedar and from Shankara to Ramana.
To call it a D2C business is to call the Ganga a water-supply company.
Let's do an honest tour of what the column missed.

The Guru: not a founder, a dispeller

"Gu" means darkness and "ru" means one who dispels it. A Guru isn't selling light. He is removing what blocks it. Sadhguru has said again and again that a Guru isn't there to give you teachings or beliefs. He is there to throw you into seeking.
The column says the customer is told the defect is in them. Sadhguru says the opposite. He says every human being is the source of their own joy and misery. That isn't a defect, it's freedom. If the problem is inside you, the solution is also inside you, and no MNC or baba can sell it to you.
That's not a business model. It's the end of one.

Sadhguru on business: money in the pocket

Now let's talk business, since the column loves it.

Sadhguru has never said money is evil. He says, "Money should be in your pocket, not in your head." He talks to CEOs at Davos, farmers in Tamil Nadu and students at IIT. He says business is simply a way of fulfilling human needs, and when business forgets human wellbeing, it becomes destructive.
He says the economic engine is powerful. Without inclusive consciousness, it will eat the planet. That's why he speaks about soil, rivers and farmers, because business should serve life, not the other way around.
Isha helps farmers form producer organisations so they get fair prices for their crops. That's business done his way: the farmer earns and the middleman doesn't.
Compare that with the column's idea of business, where everything becomes a funnel and every devotee is a data point.

The funnel that isn't one

The top of the "funnel" is free. Isha Kriya, a guided meditation, is free, and so is Upa Yoga. The Miracle of the Mind app is free. Mahashivratri is free to attend and free to stream. Anyone can sit at Adiyogi without paying a rupee.
A funnel where everything is free at the top and the bottom is not a funnel. It's a well. Anyone can draw water.
The bike is not a billboard
The column calls the motorcycle product placement. In 2022, at 64, Sadhguru rode it for about 30,000 km across 27 countries, alone, for 100 days, to ask governments to save soil. If that's product placement, the product is the planet, and it's not for sale.
Volunteers: not unpaid labour, but seva
The column calls volunteers "an unpaid workforce that pays you to work." Every Sanatani knows this word. It's called seva, and it existed long before HR departments.
At the langar in the gurudwara and the annadanam in our temples, nobody is paid and nobody is exploited. Seva isn't work. It's an offering.
Sadhguru says a volunteer is simply someone who is willing, and willingness can't be bought. Try hiring it.
Rudraksha: a bead is not just a bead
The column says a rudraksha costs ₹50 at Pooja Samagri. Maybe. A shivling is also just a stone and a temple is also just bricks.
In our tradition, prana pratishtha, consecration, changes a stone into a living force. That's why Hindus have built temples for thousands of years. We didn't build them for Instagram. We built them for energy.
Isha has also offered consecrated rudraksha free to people ahead of Mahashivratri. The column forgot to mention that.
"If you leave a guru, you lose your identity"
This is the most ignorant line in the article. The whole purpose of the Guru is to destroy your identity: your ego, your labels and your limited self. Sadhguru calls it dissolving the boundaries. A Guru doesn't give you an identity. He takes it away.
No Sanatani mother tells her child they'll go to hell for leaving a Guru. There's no hell in that sense in our tradition. The column has mixed up someone else's theology with ours.
The part the P&L can't see
There are schools for rural children, medical care in villages, trees planted on farmers' own land and rivers being revived. None of this is revenue. All of it is service.
The Guru parampara has survived invasions, colonisers and missionaries, and it will survive columnists too.
Every institution has critics. Criticise the fees if you want, and question the accounts. That's fair. But when you call the Guru a salesman and seekers customers, you aren't doing business analysis. You're mocking a civilisation.
The column is right about one thing: the Guru has insane retention. But not because of fear or guilt. When someone shows you the way inward, you don't need to be retained. You stay.
Try doing that if you're an ad agency.
Guru Brahma, Guru Vishnu, Guru Devo Maheshwara!

text:
runs into trouble. Galatians 4:25 does not say God has permanently discarded Jerusalem, cancelled Israel, and transferred every national promise to the Church. Paul himself later writes in Romans 11:1, “Hath God cast away his people? God forbid.” Romans 11:26 says, “And so all Israel shall be saved,” and verse 29 says, “For the gifts and calling of God are without repentance.” Earthly Jerusalem’s condition in Paul’s day does not erase its prophetic future. A city can be presently under judgment without God losing the deed to promises He signed with His own word.
The expression “which now is” therefore should not be ignored. Paul is speaking about present Jerusalem in contrast with the heavenly Jerusalem of the next verse. Right division requires the interpreter to respect time words as much as doctrinal words. “Now” is not “forever,” and a present spiritual condition is not automatically the cancellation of future national promises.
“and is in bondage with her children.”
Paul completes the picture by saying earthly Jerusalem “is in bondage with her children.”The bondwoman, the Sinai covenant, and present Jerusalem all line up on one side of his allegory. The children associated with that system remain under bondage because law cannot create the liberty of sonship found in Christ. The tragedy was especially sharp because men who possessed the Scriptures, temple traditions, circumcision, feast days, and the heritage of the fathers could still remain outside the liberty offered in the Messiah.
Paul knew that condition personally. Before his conversion he had been “an Hebrew of the Hebrews; as touching the law, a Pharisee”(Philippians 3:5), and “touching the righteousness which is in the law, blameless”(Philippians 3:6). Yet he counted those things loss for Christ. Religious privilege had not justified him. Heritage had not justified him. Zeal had not justified him. The law could place demands upon him, but only Christ could give him the righteousness of God by faith. A man can own an impressive religious résumé and still discover that heaven does not accept résumés in place of redemption.
The bondage in this verse is therefore not merely political Roman occupation. Paul’s entire argument concerns covenantal and spiritual bondage. Galatians 3:23 says, “before faith came, we were kept under the law, shut up unto the faith which should afterwards be revealed.” Galatians 4:3 speaks of being “in bondage under the elements of the world.”Galatians 5:1 commands believers, “be not entangled again with the yoke of bondage.”Paul is confronting an attempt to replace liberty in Christ with servant-like religious standing.
Yet the bondage does not imply that Israelites were uniquely wicked or incapable of salvation. Paul himself was an Israelite and was gloriously saved. Romans 10:1 says, “Brethren, my heart’s desire and prayer to God for Israel is, that they might be saved.” The issue is not ethnicity but the means of righteousness. A Jew trusting law cannot be justified by law any more than a Gentile trusting pagan religion can be justified by paganism. Both need Christ.
The phrase “with her children” also shows that systems reproduce their own spiritual mindset. Bondage produces bondage-thinking. A legal system teaches its children to measure themselves by performance, fear failure as though acceptance were continually at stake, and treat religious labor as though sonship were wages. Grace produces something entirely different: sons who serve because they belong, not servants trying to perform until somebody agrees to adopt them. Legalism hands the child a timesheet; grace hands him the family name.

“We didn’t discuss it”: Trump rejects claim he offered to sell arms to Xi

US President Donald Trump on Monday denied asking Chinese President Xi Jinping if he wanted to buy American weapons, contradicting his own envoy’s claim.

US Ambassador to China David Perdue told Fox News on Sunday that Trump made the offer during Xi’s White House state visit last week, in response to Chinese concerns over US arms sales to Taiwan.

Asked about the remarks in the Oval Office, Trump told reporters, “I’ve never heard of that one, I’m going to have to ask him.”

He added, “They’d probably like to buy it because we do make better equipment than them, so maybe it’s a good idea. But we didn’t discuss it.”

A US official told Yahoo via AFP that “the US government has no plans to sell weapons to China.” The State Department said US law prohibits arms sales to China.

China’s foreign ministry did not directly answer when asked about the comments.

Trump has declined to say whether Taiwan was discussed. The two leaders will meet again at the APEC summit in Shenzhen in November and the G20 in Miami in December.

text:
Experimental evidence of altermagnetism in a layered material opens a promising path toward future spintronics

28SEP2026
By Andrew Miller, University of Central Florida
edited by Robert Egan
https://t.co/IfBnGZimkS

To build the ultrafast computers of the future, scientists are looking beyond the electrical charge of electrons to another property: their spin. While conventional hardware relies on the movement of charge to process data, tapping into this intrinsic quantum property could enable researchers to reinvent how information travels through a circuit.

Now, a team led by UCF physics professor Madhab Neupane has identified a promising candidate. Neupane and his collaborators found evidence of altermagnetism, an emerging form of magnetism that combines useful characteristics of two more familiar types: ferromagnetism and antiferromagnetism.

Their paper is published in the journal Nature Communications.
https://t.co/u9GY8KvIJa

Ferromagnetism produces the behavior most people associate with everyday magnets. In these materials, magnetic moments align in the same direction, creating a magnetic field. That property can be useful in electronics, but the resulting stray magnetic fields can interfere with nearby components.

Antiferromagnets behave differently. Their magnetic moments point in opposing directions and cancel one another out, largely avoiding stray fields. However, they lack some of the useful electronic properties found in ferromagnets.

Altermagnets offer another possibility by combining desirable characteristics of both.

Like antiferromagnets, they can avoid producing unwanted stray magnetic fields. But they can also generate and detect spin currents—the movement of electron spins through a material—that researchers hope to use for future electronics.

Neupane and his collaborators experimentally identified signatures of this unusual magnetic state in Co₁/₄TaSe₂, a layered material containing magnetic cobalt atoms. The discovery gives researchers a versatile platform for studying altermagnetism and could help advance future electronic and spintronic technologies.

"These materials are distinguished from more conventional antiferromagnets by their ability to generate and detect spin currents without the negative effect of producing stray fields," Neupane says. "This new property makes them very well positioned for use in many different applications—including spintronics, ultrafast memory devices, terahertz networks and energy-efficient electronics."

Tracking the signs of altermagnetism
To determine whether Co₁/₄TaSe₂ exhibited altermagnetism, the researchers needed to examine how its electrons behaved.

They used a technique called angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy, or ARPES, which allows scientists to measure the energy and movement of electrons and map a material's electronic structure.

"Our approach was to use higher-resolution methods that were insensitive to the electron's spin to measure the splitting in the energy levels," Neupane says. "Then, we complemented this measurement with spin-resolved ARPES to conclusively tell if this looks like altermagnetism."

The team first detected a characteristic splitting in the material's electronic bands. They then used spin-resolved ARPES to take a closer look and found that those split states carried opposite spin polarizations, key evidence of altermagnetism.

Getting a clear look at that behavior presented another challenge. Photoemission measurements are extremely sensitive to a material's surface, so researchers needed exceptionally clean samples to accurately observe what was happening.

While collaborators produced high-quality Co₁/₄TaSe₂ samples, Neupane's team carefully screened them for ultraclean surfaces before mapping the material's electronic behavior.

"The significance became clear once the experimental measurements consistently matched our theoretical predictions," Neupane says. "Seeing those independent pieces of evidence converge gave us confidence that we had identified a genuine layered altermagnet."

Why layered materials are changing the game
Finding evidence of altermagnetism was only part of what made Co₁/₄TaSe₂ interesting to researchers.

The material is built from extremely thin layers stacked on top of one another. Because those layers are weakly bound, scientists can separate and combine them into extremely thin structures, making layered materials promising for use in thin-film devices and other emerging technologies.

Scientists call this family of layered materials transition-metal dichalcogenides, or TMDs.

In Co₁/₄TaSe₂, magnetic cobalt atoms inserted between the layers help create the material's unusual magnetic properties. Its layered structure also makes the material highly tunable, allowing researchers to modify it and study how those changes affect its electronic and magnetic behavior.

The team also wanted to understand where that unusual electronic behavior originated. Before the study, it was unclear whether the key signatures of altermagnetism in layered materials would come primarily from the surface or from deeper within the material.

Their measurements showed that the relevant electronic state originated primarily within the material itself and displayed clear signatures of altermagnetic order.

"Evidence for altermagnetism in a versatile materials platform opens a lot of new possibilities," says Milo Sprague, the study's lead graduate student researcher. edited by Robert Egan

To build the ultrafast computers of the future, scientists are looking beyond the electrical charge of electrons to another property: their spin. While conventional hardware relies on the movement of charge to process data, tapping into this intrinsic quantum property could enable researchers to reinvent how information travels through a circuit.

Now, a team led by UCF physics professor Madhab Neupane has identified a promising candidate. Neupane and his collaborators found evidence of altermagnetism, an emerging form of magnetism that combines useful characteristics of two more familiar types: ferromagnetism and antiferromagnetism. 

Their paper is published in the journal Nature Communications.
https://t.co/u9GY8KvIJa

Ferromagnetism produces the behavior most people associate with everyday magnets. In these materials, magnetic moments align in the same direction, creating a magnetic field. That property can be useful in electronics, but the resulting stray magnetic fields can interfere with nearby components.

Antiferromagnets behave differently. Their magnetic moments point in opposing directions and cancel one another out, largely avoiding stray fields. However, they lack some of the useful electronic properties found in ferromagnets.

Altermagnets offer another possibility by combining desirable characteristics of both.

Like antiferromagnets, they can avoid producing unwanted stray magnetic fields. But they can also generate and detect spin currents—the movement of electron spins through a material—that researchers hope to use for future electronics.

Neupane and his collaborators experimentally identified signatures of this unusual magnetic state in Co₁/₄TaSe₂, a layered material containing magnetic cobalt atoms. The discovery gives researchers a versatile platform for studying altermagnetism and could help advance future electronic and spintronic technologies.

"These materials are distinguished from more conventional antiferromagnets by their ability to generate and detect spin currents without the negative effect of producing stray fields," Neupane says. "This new property makes them very well positioned for use in many different applications—including spintronics, ultrafast memory devices, terahertz networks and energy-efficient electronics."

To determine whether Co₁/₄TaSe₂ exhibited altermagnetism, the researchers needed to examine how its electrons behaved.

They used a technique called angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy, or ARPES, which allows scientists to measure the energy and movement of electrons and map a material's electronic structure.

"Our approach was to use higher-resolution methods that were insensitive to the electron's spin to measure the splitting in the energy levels," Neupane says. "Then, we complemented this measurement with spin-resolved ARPES to conclusively tell if this looks like altermagnetism."

The team first detected a characteristic splitting in the material's electronic bands. They then used spin-resolved ARPES to take a closer look and found that those split states carried opposite spin polarizations, key evidence of altermagnetism.

Getting a clear look at that behavior presented another challenge. Photoemission measurements are extremely sensitive to a material's surface, so researchers needed exceptionally clean samples to accurately observe what was happening.

While collaborators produced high-quality Co₁/₄TaSe₂ samples, Neupane's team carefully screened them for ultraclean surfaces before mapping the material's electronic behavior.

The material is built from extremely thin layers stacked on top of one another. Because those layers are weakly bound, scientists can separate and combine them into extremely thin structures, making layered materials promising for use in thin-film devices and other emerging technologies.

Scientists call this family of layered materials transition-metal dichalcogenides, or TMDs.

In Co₁/₄TaSe₂, magnetic cobalt atoms inserted between the layers help create the material's unusual magnetic properties. Its layered structure also makes the material highly tunable, allowing researchers to modify it and study how those changes affect its electronic and magnetic behavior.

The team also wanted to understand where that unusual electronic behavior originated. Before the study, it was unclear whether the key signatures of altermagnetism in layered materials would come primarily from the surface or from deeper within the material.

Their measurements showed that the relevant electronic state originated primarily within the material itself and displayed clear signatures of altermagnetic order.

"There's currently a lot of debate in altermagnetic theory about how the spin-polarized electronic states interact with other magnetic phenomena. "If this approach proves viable, then layered altermagnets will be at the forefront of electronics development," Neupane says.

The vile pope is uniting the entire world to turn against the humble tiny minority that keep the true Bible Sabbath like Charlie Kirk did.  The world will wake up, but it will be too late to escape the snare.  With every rejection of truth the minds of the people will become darker, their hearts more stubborn, until they are entrenched in an infidel hardihood. In defiance of the warnings which God has given, they will continue to trample upon one of the precepts of the Decalogue, until they are led to persecute those who hold it sacred. Christ is set at nought in the contempt placed upon His word and His people. As the teachings of spiritualism are accepted by the churches, the restraint imposed upon the carnal heart is removed, and the profession of religion will become a cloak to conceal the basest iniquity. A belief in spiritual manifestations opens the door to seducing spirits and doctrines of devils, and thus the influence of evil angels will be felt in the churches.
Fearful is the issue to which the world is to be brought. The powers of earth, uniting to war against the commandments of God, will decree that “all, both small and great, rich and poor, free and bond” ( Revelation 13:16), shall conform to the customs of the church by the observance of the false sabbath. All who refuse compliance will be visited with civil penalties, and it will finally be declared that they are deserving of death. On the other hand, the law of God enjoining the Creator’s rest day demands obedience and threatens wrath against all who transgress its precepts. With the issue thus clearly brought before him, whoever shall trample upon God’s law to obey a human enactment receives the mark of the beast; he accepts the sign of allegiance to the power which he chooses to obey instead of God. The warning from heaven is: “If any man worship the beast and his image, and receive his mark in his forehead, or in his hand, the same shall drink of the wine of the wrath of God, which is poured out without mixture into the cup of His indignation.” Revelation 14:9, 10. 
But not one is made to suffer the wrath of God until the truth has been brought home to his mind and conscience, and has been rejected. There are many who have never had an opportunity to hear the special truths for this time. The obligation of the fourth commandment has never been set before them in its true light. He who reads every heart and tries every motive will leave none who desire a knowledge of the truth, to be deceived as to the issues of the controversy. The decree is not to be urged upon the people blindly. Everyone is to have sufficient light to make his decision intelligently. 
The Sabbath will be the great test of loyalty, for it is the point of truth especially controverted. When the final test shall be brought to bear upon men, then the line of distinction will be drawn between those who serve God and those who serve Him not. While the observance of the false sabbath in compliance with the law of the state, contrary to the fourth commandment, will be an avowal of allegiance to a power that is in opposition to God, the keeping of the true Sabbath, in obedience to God’s law, is an evidence of loyalty to the Creator. While one class, by accepting the sign of submission to earthly powers, receive the mark of the beast, the other choosing the token of allegiance to divine authority, receive the seal of God. 
 As the time comes for it to be given with greatest power, the Lord will work through humble instruments, leading the minds of those who consecrate themselves to His service. The laborers will be qualified rather by the unction of His Spirit than by the training of literary institutions. Men of faith and prayer will be constrained to go forth with holy zeal, declaring the words which God gives them. The sins of Babylon will be laid open. The fearful results of enforcing the observances of the church by civil authority, the inroads of spiritualism, the stealthy but rapid progress of the papal power—all will be unmasked. By these solemn warnings the people will be stirred. Thousands upon thousands will listen who have never heard words like these. In amazement they hear the testimony that Babylon is the church, fallen because of her errors and sins, because of her rejection of the truth sent to her from heaven. As the people go to their former teachers with the eager inquiry, Are these things so? the ministers present fables, prophesy smooth things, to soothe their fears and quiet the awakened conscience. But since many refuse to be satisfied with the mere authority of men and demand a plain “Thus saith the Lord,” the popular ministry, like the Pharisees of old, filled with anger as their authority is questioned, will denounce the message as of Satan and stir up the sin-loving multitudes to revile and persecute those who proclaim it.
As the controversy extends into new fields and the minds of the people are called to God’s downtrodden law, Satan is astir. The power attending the message will only madden those who oppose it. The clergy will put forth almost superhuman efforts to shut away the light lest it should shine upon their flocks. By every means at their command they will endeavor to suppress the discussion of these vital questions. The church appeals to the strong arm of civil power, and, in this work, papists and Protestants unite. As the movement for Sunday enforcement becomes more bold and decided, the law will be invoked against commandment keepers. They will be threatened with fines and imprisonment, and some will be offered positions of influence, and other rewards and advantages, as inducements to renounce their faith. But their steadfast answer is: “Show us from the word of God our error”—the same plea that was made by Luther under similar circumstances. Those who are arraigned before the courts make a strong vindication of the truth, and some who hear them are led to take their stand to keep all the commandments of God. Thus light will be brought before thousands who otherwise would know nothing of these truths.

When He leaves the sanctuary, darkness covers the inhabitants of the earth. In that fearful time the righteous must live in the sight of a holy God without an intercessor. The restraint which has been upon the wicked is removed, and Satan has entire control of the finally impenitent. God’s long-suffering has ended. The world has rejected His mercy, despised His love, and trampled upon His law. The wicked have passed the boundary of their probation; the Spirit of God, persistently resisted, has been at last withdrawn. Unsheltered by divine grace, they have no protection from the wicked one. Satan will then plunge the inhabitants of the earth into one great, final trouble. As the angels of God cease to hold in check the fierce winds of human passion, all the elements of strife will be let loose. The whole world will be involved in ruin more terrible than that which came upon Jerusalem of old.
As the Sabbath has become the special point of controversy throughout Christendom, and religious and secular authorities have combined to enforce the observance of the Sunday, the persistent refusal of a small minority to yield to the popular demand will make them objects of universal execration. It will be urged that the few who stand in opposition to an institution of the church and a law of the state ought not to be tolerated; that it is better for them to suffer than for whole nations to be thrown into confusion and lawlessness. The same argument many centuries ago was brought against Christ by the “rulers of the people.” “It is expedient for us,” said the wily Caiaphas, “that one man should die for the people, and that the whole nation perish not.” John 11:50. This argument will appear conclusive; and a decree will finally be issued against those who hallow the Sabbath of the fourth commandment, denouncing them as deserving of the severest punishment and giving
the people liberty, after a certain time, to put them to death. Romanism in the Old World and apostate Protestantism in the New will pursue a similar course toward those who honor all the divine precepts. 
The people of God will then be plunged into those scenes of affliction and distress described by the prophet as the time of Jacob’s trouble. “Thus saith the Lord: We have heard a voice of trembling, of fear, and not of peace.... All faces are turned into paleness. Alas! for that day is great, so that none is like it: it is even the time of Jacob’s trouble; but he shall be saved out of it.” Jeremiah 30:5-7.

Prison

The most dangerous bondage in Galatians was not built without Scripture; it was built with Scripture mishandled. That is what makes doctrinal error so deceptive. Anybody can recognize an argument that says, “Forget the Bible.” The harder danger is the man who says, “The Bible says,” quotes something accurately, and then applies it inaccurately. Satan himself quoted Scripture to Jesus Christ in Matthew 4. The quotation did not become false merely because Satan spoke it. The devil’s use of it was false because Scripture was being weaponized outside its proper application.

This is why 2 Timothy 2:15 does not merely command study; it commands “rightly dividing the word of truth.” Notice what is being divided rightly: truth. Error is not the only thing that can be mishandled. Truth can be put in the wrong place. Noah was truthfully commanded to build an ark. Abraham was truthfully commanded to offer Isaac. Israel was truthfully commanded to bring animal sacrifices. Priests were truthfully commanded to perform Levitical duties. A man who takes those commands and applies them directly to the Church today has not become “more biblical” because every sentence he quotes appears in Scripture. A verse can be perfectly inspired and perfectly quoted while being perfectly misapplied.

Religious bondage thrives on that confusion. One group finds a command to Israel and imposes it upon the Church. Another finds kingdom instructions and confuses them with justification. Another takes a discipleship warning and uses it to overturn eternal security. Another takes a passage about reward and makes it about receiving eternal life. The Book remains right while the interpreter turns the wiring backward and wonders why the lights go out. The cure is not less Bible but more careful Bible. False doctrine often begins when a true verse is delivered to the wrong address.

7. Christ Breaks The Chains Religion Polishes

Paul’s answer to bondage is not religious anarchy. It is Jesus Christ. Galatians 5:1 declares, “Stand fast therefore in the liberty wherewith Christ hath made us free.” Notice who made the believer free: Christ. Liberty is not something the Christian manufactures through emotional confidence. It rests upon an objective work completed outside him by the Son of God. Christ was “made under the law, To redeem them that were under the law” (Galatians 4:4–5). He did not redeem men by pretending the law’s righteous demands did not matter. He fulfilled righteousness and bore the curse.

Galatians 3:13 says, “Christ hath redeemed us from the curse of the law, being made a curse for us.” That is substitution. Somebody bore the judgment. Somebody paid the price. Somebody stood where the guilty deserved to stand. At Calvary, grace did not bribe justice or sneak around the courthouse after dark. The sinless Son of God became the lawful Substitute for sinners. God did not bend righteousness to save the sinner; He satisfied righteousness in the Saviour.

That is why adding religious bondage after Calvary is such a serious doctrinal insult. If Christ paid the account, stop sliding pennies under heaven’s door as though the receipt were questionable. If Christ redeemed the prisoner, stop explaining that spiritual maturity requires sleeping inside the old cell on weekends. If Christ gave sonship, stop making sons think like hired servants. Colossians 2:10 says believers are “complete in him.” The Christian life certainly involves growth, correction, obedience, service, suffering, discipline, and reward, but none of those things becomes a supplement to Christ’s sufficiency for standing. Religion spends centuries polishing chains; Christ walks into the prison, opens the door, and asks why redeemed men are still admiring the lock.
