text:
FLP BOOK OF THE DAY: Fragile Intersect by Lynn Kincanon
 
On SALE:    https://t.co/3YCZ04FCsQ
 
Fragile Intersect operates with the steady hand of an observer who knows the rhythm of the human heart—both its biological fragility and its emotional resilience. Drawing from thirty-six years specializing in cardiology at the bedside of Emergency Room, ICU, and Telemetry Units, Lynn Kincanon offers a rare clarity, seeking a respite for the soul through steadfast observation and sharp, detailed imagery.  At its core, Fragile Intersect is a contribution to the established Medical Humanities and emerging field of Lyric Medicine. It is a vital exploration of healing, trauma, and the transition from a life of service to the freedom of retirement. By the final poem, the author has begun her own “transformation from autumn’s color to whiteness,” leaving the reader with a profound sense of gratitude for the journey traveled. #Medical  #Poetry  #WomenPoets  #NaturePoetry #Ecopoetry 
 
Lynn Kincanon is a poet of steadfast observation whose work pulses with “lyrical lifeforce energy.” As the Poet Laureate of Loveland, Colorado Emerita  (2022–2025), she is a defining presence in the contemporary poetry scene of Northern Colorado, recognized for a style that balances nature-infused imagery with profound emotional resonance. Her writing offers a rare clarity informed by a distinguished thirty-six-year career in nursing and as a Nurse Practitioner specializing in cardiac care, allowing her to monitor the human heart through a dual lens of clinical precision and soulful evocativeness. A dedicated mentor and collaborator, Lynn is the author of two chapbooks, Evocation, and Art as Metaphor, Analogy and Allegory (self-published 2013) and the forthcoming collection, Fragile Intersect (Finishing Line Press 2026).  @lynnkincanon   Website: https://t.co/1WpmxJWH5R
 
PRAISE:
.
These poems listen for the moment when the body’s capacity to be a body falters or resumes. With care, Kincanon’s poems evoke the life-world of the one whose work it is to nurse, equally so: “Stepping over the threshold,/ I feel a tender swaying.”  This instinct towards pendulation is carried through the collection, which alternates between the ward, and the plush liminality of the natural world. Transcribing, owl “hoots,” a “ridgeline” coyote glimpsed  in the browning grass, the bright flash of a heron plucking a koi from the garden pond, the poet-nurse restores her own being, a form of soft attention that functions as an antidote, medicine in its own right.
–Bhanu Kapil
.
Fragile Intersect, indeed! These poems straddle grittiness and gratefulness, blue sky and Code Blue, honeysuckle berries and the ICU, listening to birdsong and the heart’s faithful lub dub, lub dub. I love these poems that point equally to our mortality and to the great gift of life. Perceptive, compassionate, and lyrical, these are clear-eyed, open-hearted invitations to be as present and vulnerable in our lives as this remarkable nurse poet.
–Rosemerry Wahtola Trommer, author of The Unfolding and host of The Poetic Path
.
Fragile Intersect is a debut poetry collection that listens closely at the crossing of life and loss. Drawing on years as a poet and former cardiac nurse, Lynn Kincanon writes with a clear-eyed tenderness shaped by hospital rooms, mountain mornings, and the quiet urgencies that arrive when time feels finite. I love how these poems attend to crickets before the freeze, fog-draped moons, parting blessings, and the beauty we leave behind. With language that is compassionate but unsentimental, Fragile Intersect embodies what it means to live more mindfully and to count what matters. With sensory richness and surprising turns of thought, these moving poems stand at the intersection where mortality sharpens gratitude.
–Evan Oakley, M.A.,MFA Professor Emeritus.  English, Communications, Literature Department Aims Community College.

I understand you perspective but don't see where it says or even implies that the suspension  of "sacrifice and offerings" is a violation of the covenant. That must be read into the text. 

Consider the Hebrew phrase זבח ומנחה (sacrifice and offering) used here in Daniel 9:27 . This exact phrase is used only three times in the Bible (Psalm 40:7, Isaiah 19:212, Daniel 9:27).  There is a fourth time the exact spelling of the words are used together but the order of the words is reversed (Lev. 23:37).

Yahweh inspired king David to use this exact phrase in Psalm 40 as a prophetic picture of Jesus and his sacrifice that once and for all ended the sacrifice and offering required in the Torah. 

 In fact the author of Hebrews quotes Psalm 40 when he makes the case that Jesus ended the necessity for the sacrificial system. 

Psalm 40:1-2, 6-7, 16-17
I waited patiently for YHWH; and he inclined unto me, and heard my cry. He brought me up also out of an horrible pit, out of the miry clay, and set my feet upon a rock, and established my goings…

Sacrifice and offering [זבח ומנחה] thou didst not desire; mine ears hast thou opened: burnt offering and sin offering hast thou not required.

Then said I, Lo, I come: in the volume of the book it is written of me,

…Let all those that seek thee rejoice and be glad in thee: let such as love thy salvation say continually, YHWH be magnified. But I am poor and needy; yet the Lord thinketh upon me: thou art my help and my deliverer; make no tarrying, O my God.

Hebrews 10:1-12 
 For the law having a shadow of good things to come, and not the very image of the things, can never with those sacrifices which they offered year by year continually make the comers thereunto perfect. 2 For then would they not have ceased to be offered? 
because that the worshippers once purged should have had no more conscience of sins. 
3But in those sacrifices there is a remembrance again made of sins every year. 
4 For it is not possible that the blood of bulls and of goats should take away sins. 
5 Wherefore when he cometh into the world, he saith,

Sacrifice and offering  [זבח ומנחה] thou wouldest not, but a body hast thou prepared me: 

6 In burnt offerings and sacrifices for sin thou hast had no pleasure. 7 Then said I, Lo, I come (in the volume of the book it is written of me,) to do thy will, O God.

8 Above when he said, Sacrifice and offering [זבח ומנחה] and burnt offerings and offering for sin thou wouldest not, neither hadst pleasure therein; which are offered by the law; 
9Then said he, Lo, I come to do thy will, O God. He taketh away the first, that he may establish the second. 10By the which will we are sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all. 

11 And every priest standeth daily ministering and offering oftentimes the same sacrifices, which can never take away sins: 
12 But this man, after he had offered one sacrifice for sins for ever, sat down on the right hand of God; -

text:
The most powerful bite in the entire cat family belongs to the animal in this video.

Look at that coat for eight seconds. Then read this thread-length post before you hit replay, because what you think you're looking at is only half the story.

I've spent years studying what makes content stop a thumb mid-scroll. This animal breaks every rule I know. It doesn't need a hook. It IS the hook. Evolution spent about three million years engineering it, and the result is so absurdly over-built that scientists still argue about which part is the most extreme.

So here's the full breakdown. Every number below is real. Every claim is something you can check. By the end, you will never look at this animal the same way, and you'll watch that video again with different eyes.

Let's go.

THE BITE THAT SHOULDN'T EXIST

Most big cats kill by suffocation. They clamp the throat, hold on, and wait. It works, it's efficient, and it's what tigers and lions do.

The jaguar looked at that method and said no.

Jaguars are famous for a different technique: they go straight through the skull. Documented kills show a canine tooth punched between the ears of the prey, into the brain, ending the fight in a heartbeat. No long struggle. No drama. One decision, one bite.

Relative to body size, the jaguar has the strongest bite of any big cat. Researchers who measured skull mechanics found a head built like a bank vault: short, broad, wrapped in massive jaw muscle, with a bite force estimated well above 1,000 PSI. For scale, an average human bites at roughly 160 PSI.

Read that again. This animal bites with several times the force you can, from a head not much bigger than a basketball.

And that's before we talk about what it chooses to bite.

IT BITES THROUGH ARMOR

Skulls are the easy part. Jaguars hunt animals that wear armor for a living.

Caimans, the crocodile relatives of South America, have bony plates embedded in their skin. Turtles carry a shell that evolved specifically to stop predators like this one. Armadillos are basically a small tank with legs.

Jaguars eat all three.

There are documented cases of jaguars puncturing turtle shells and taking caimans in the water. Most predators see a shell and walk away. The jaguar sees a lunch box with a lid it can open by force.

This is why the cat has such a short, heavy, almost bulldog-like skull compared to leopards. The face isn't cute by accident. It's a tool. Every curve of that head is structural, designed to transmit force from massive jaw muscles straight into the tips of the canines.

Nature does not build a machine this specialized for a casual life.

THE NAME IS A WARNING

The word "jaguar" traces back to indigenous South American languages, from a term commonly translated as "he who kills with one leap" or "the beast that kills in a single bound."

Think about that. The people who lived next to this animal for thousands of years didn't name it after its beauty. They didn't name it after its color or its size. They named it after its efficiency.

Not "the big spotted one." Not "the golden cat."

The one who ends it in one move.

Every culture names things by what matters most to survival. When your name is a description of how you kill, you have a reputation problem or a reputation triumph, depending on which side of the food chain you're standing on.

YOUR EYES DON'T LIE: THE PATTERN IS A FINGERPRINT

Look at the spots again. Not casually. Really look.

Those aren't spots. They're rosettes: broken rings of dark marks, and this is the detail that separates a jaguar from every other spotted cat. Inside many of the rosettes there are smaller dark dots, like a bullseye with a nucleus.

Leopards have rosettes too. Their rosettes are smaller, more tightly packed, and usually empty inside. Jaguar rosettes are larger, bolder, fewer in number, and often carry those inner spots.

Here's what makes it wild: no two jaguars share the same pattern. Field researchers use this to identify individual animals from camera trap photos. Just as a detective matches fingerprints, biologists match rosette maps. A cat photographed in one year can be recognized again years later, purely by the geometry of its coat.

The animal in front of you is a one-of-one. There has never been another pattern exactly like it, and there never will be.

THE COAT ISN'T DECORATION, IT'S ENGINEERING

Why the rosettes? Because the jaguar hunts in dappled light.

Rainforest floors, riverbanks, dense scrub: places where sunlight arrives in broken fragments through leaves. A solid golden coat would glow in that environment. A rosetted coat dissolves into it.

The pattern breaks up the outline of the body. The eye of the prey, or a prey animal's brain, has trouble reading "predator shape" when the edges are scrambled into dozens of contrasting patches. It's camouflage that works through disruption rather than blending.

Move the animal into open savanna and it looks conspicuous. Put it back in the forest edge at dusk and it vanishes. The coat is a piece of environmental software, tuned by millions of years of trial and error, and it only makes sense in its home.

What looks like the most beautiful feature is actually the most lethal one. It gets the cat close enough to use the bite.

NOT A LEOPARD. NOT EVEN CLOSE.

The internet mixes these two up constantly. Let's fix that permanently.

Leopards live in Africa and Asia. Jaguars live in the Americas. Different continents, different evolutionary stories.

Leopards are lean, long-limbed, built for climbing and sneaking. Jaguars are stocky, heavily muscled, shorter-legged, built for power. If a leopard is a sprinter, a jaguar is a heavyweight boxer.

Jaguars are typically larger and considerably heavier. Big males in some regions push past 100 kilograms, and exceptional individuals have been recorded even heavier. That makes the jaguar the third-largest cat on Earth, behind only the tiger and the lion, and the largest cat in the Americas by a wide margin.

The cougar, its main rival on the continent, is lighter and lankier. When the two share territory, the jaguar takes the heavier prey, and the ecosystem quietly reorganizes around that fact.

THE BLACK PANTHER IS A LIE (SORT OF)

Here's the question that gets asked in every comment section: is a "black panther" a separate species?

No. There's no such species.

A black panther is simply a leopard or a jaguar with melanism, a genetic condition that produces excess dark pigment. Both cats can be born black. In jaguars, roughly one in ten animals carries the dark coat in some populations.

Now the twist that surprises people: in jaguars, the black coat is caused by a dominant gene. In leopards, it's recessive. Same visual result, opposite inheritance rules, arrived at independently. Evolution solved "make it dark" twice using two different mechanisms.

And the spots never actually disappear. In bright light, you can still see the rosettes ghosting through the black fur, like a watermark. The pattern is always there. It's simply written in a darker ink.

Some researchers think black coats may offer advantages in dense, dark forest. The debate continues. Nobody has all the answers yet.

IT IS THE CAT THAT LOVES WATER

Most house cats treat a bathtub like a hostile act. The jaguar treats a river like a hunting ground.

It swims well, and it swims willingly. Across the Pantanal wetlands of Brazil and the rivers of the Amazon basin, jaguars cross channels, patrol riverbanks, and take prey directly out of the water. Fish, capybara, caiman, even large snakes have been recorded on the menu.

No other big cat in the world is this comfortable in aquatic environments to this degree. Tigers like water too, but the jaguar lives in a world where water is the main highway and the main pantry.

This is a huge part of why it's considered the apex predator of its region. It isn't dominant in one habitat. It's dominant across three: forest, floodplain, and river.

Ask yourself: what other animal can ambush you from the treeline, the shoreline, and the current?

THE SEA TURTLE HUNTER

Here's a fact that sounds made up.

On certain beaches in Central America, jaguars have been documented walking out of the forest at night to hunt nesting sea turtles. A female turtle hauls herself up the sand to lay eggs, slow, heavy, protected by a shell, and a jaguar steps out of the treeline to meet her.

Researchers working on protected coastlines have recorded the evidence: turtle carcasses on the beach with the shells cracked open and the meat taken.

Think about the scene. A rainforest predator, on a beach, at night, hunting an ocean animal that only comes ashore a few times in its life. It's a collision of two ecosystems that shouldn't touch, and this cat is the one who bridges them.

It's one of the strangest predator behaviors ever filmed, and it happens on real, ordinary-looking beaches.

SILENT MATH: HOW AN AMBUSH ACTUALLY WORKS

Jaguars are not chase hunters. They're ambush specialists.

A cheetah runs its prey down in a burst of speed measured in miles per hour. A jaguar does the opposite. It moves slowly, deliberately, close to the ground, using cover as a weapon. It stalks until the distance is small enough that a single explosive lunge finishes the job.

The calculation it's running is simple and brutal: energy in versus energy out. A failed chase wastes calories. A successful ambush pays for days. So the animal invests in patience, hides in vegetation or shadow, waits for the moment when the odds tilt overwhelmingly, and then commits everything.

That's what makes those muscles matter. The thick shoulders, the powerful forelimbs, the dense chest are all built for a few seconds of overwhelming force, not long-distance stamina. This is a sprinter's engine tuned for one perfect explosion.

Patience is a weapon. The jaguar proves it.

HOW BIG IS "BIG"?

Let's put numbers on this so your brain can actually process it.

Adult jaguars generally weigh somewhere between 55 and 100 kilograms depending on region, with males considerably heavier than females. The largest individuals, especially in the Pantanal, are famous for their bulk.

In the wetlands, where prey like caiman and capybara is abundant, jaguars grow bigger than their cousins in the dense rainforests of Central America. Same species, different environment, different body size. It's a classic case of habitat shaping anatomy.

To picture it: think of a large adult human. Now imagine an animal roughly comparable in mass, but with zero body fat that isn't functional, compressed into a low, wide frame, with a tail and a skull that belong in an engineering textbook.

It doesn't look enormous from far away. Cats deceive the eye. It looks enormous only when you're close enough for it to matter.

THE LONELY KING

Jaguars live alone. Nearly always.

Lions have prides. Wolves have packs. Even many smaller cats come with social lives. The jaguar has a territory, a patrol route, and occasionally a mate for a short window of time. That's about it.

Each animal maintains a large home range, marking it with scent, scrapes, and vocalizations to let neighbors know the address is taken. A male's territory typically overlaps with several females, and the size depends heavily on how much food the land can provide. Richer habitat, smaller range. Poorer habitat, much bigger.

This isolation shapes everything about its behavior. There's no backup in a fight. There's no team to share the risk. Every hunt is a solo operation, and any serious injury can be the beginning of the end.

That's why it plays the game so carefully. Being the top predator doesn't mean being reckless. It means being the one who almost never gets hurt.

THE SOUND

Jaguars roar. Not all cats can.

The ability to roar belongs to the genus Panthera: lions, tigers, leopards, and jaguars. It's tied to the anatomy of the larynx and the ligaments around it, which allow deep, resonant, low-frequency sound.

The jaguar's vocal repertoire is surprisingly wide. It includes a deep roar, a rasping cough-like call, and a strange, rhythmic sawing sound that people often compare to someone cutting wood. Females use calls to communicate with males, and males use them to claim territory.

In a rainforest at night, sound travels differently than it does on open grassland. Low-frequency calls carry farther through dense vegetation. The animal isn't shouting. It's broadcasting on a frequency the forest carries well.

If you ever hear that sound in person, you'll never forget it.

THE EYES OF A NIGHT PREDATOR

Jaguars are most active at dusk, dawn, and through the night. Their eyes are built for it.

Like most cats, they have a reflective layer behind the retina called the tapetum lucidum. It acts like a mirror, bouncing light back through the retina a second time and dramatically boosting sensitivity in low light. It's why cat eyes glow when a flashlight hits them.

Add oversized pupils that open wide in darkness and a high density of light-sensitive rod cells, and the result is vision that operates comfortably in conditions where a human would be stumbling.

But sight is only part of the package. Whiskers detect air movement and near-field obstacles. Ears swivel to isolate direction. Smell adds a layer of chemical information that we can barely imagine.

When people say a predator "senses" its environment, this is what they mean. Not one super-sense. A stack of them, layered together, feeding a brain that decides in fractions of a second.

173,000 AND FALLING

Now the part that should make you uncomfortable.

A widely cited scientific estimate puts the wild jaguar population at roughly 173,000 animals across the entire Americas. That sounds like a lot until you spread it across a range that stretches from Mexico to Argentina. Then it starts to look thin.

Historically, jaguars roamed far more widely, from the southwestern United States to the southern tip of the continent. Over the past century they've lost roughly half of that original range. They're gone from El Salvador and Uruguay. In the United States they persist only as rare visitors, like the famous wild male nicknamed El Jefe, filmed in the mountains of Arizona.

The species is classified as Near Threatened, which is the polite phrase for "we are one bad decade away from something worse."

The largest cat in the Americas, the apex of an entire continent, is now competing for space with cattle ranches, roads, and cities.

WHAT'S ACTUALLY KILLING THEM

The threats aren't mysterious. They're painfully ordinary.

Deforestation is the biggest driver. Every hectare of forest converted to farmland is territory removed from the map. Cats need connected habitat to hunt, mate, and disperse. When you chop the forest into isolated islands, populations become trapped, inbred, and vulnerable.

Conflict with ranchers is the second big factor. When natural prey declines and cattle fill the landscape, jaguars sometimes take livestock, and retaliation follows. A single predator can be shot in response to a single loss.

Then there's poaching. Skins, teeth, and claws have all been traded, and demand for jaguar parts has increased in some regions as supplies of other big cat products have dwindled.

None of these threats are dramatic. They're slow, bureaucratic, economic. That's exactly why they're so deadly. Extinction rarely arrives with a bang. It arrives with a permit.

THE 18-COUNTRY HIGHWAY

Here's the part that gives me hope.

Conservationists launched a bold idea: connect jaguar habitat across the entire continent. The concept is often called the Jaguar Corridor, a chain of protected areas and wildlife-friendly landscapes stretching across around eighteen countries, letting cats move, breed, and spread their genes.

Think about how ambitious that is. It means governments, ranchers, indigenous communities, scientists, and local landowners agreeing on a shared map for an animal that doesn't understand borders.

It works because the jaguar is what ecologists call an umbrella species. Protect enough land for a jaguar, and you automatically protect thousands of other species living beneath it: birds, fish, monkeys, amphibians, plants. Save the top predator and you save the architecture of the whole system.

It's the most efficient conservation strategy on Earth, and its logo has spots.

WHY THE PREDATOR MATTERS MORE THAN THE PREY

There's a concept in ecology called a trophic cascade, and jaguars are a textbook example of why it matters.

Remove a top predator, and the herbivores below it start to boom. Too many of them eat too much vegetation. Seedlings never mature. Forest composition changes. Soil erodes. Smaller predators multiply and hammer smaller prey. The damage spreads through the system like a crack through glass.

Keep the top predator in place, and the pressure stays balanced. Prey species remain wary and mobile, which prevents overgrazing in any one spot. Mid-sized predators stay in check. The ecosystem holds its shape.

That's the quiet job of the animal in this video. It isn't only a hunter. It's a regulator, a thermostat for an entire forest. Losing it doesn't merely remove one species. It rewires everything that used to depend on it.

THE GOD IN THE JUNGLE

Long before conservation biology, people already understood how special this animal is.

The Olmec civilization, among the earliest complex societies in Mesoamerica, carved figures blending human and feline features, so-called "were-jaguar" imagery that appears in art thousands of years old. The Maya associated the jaguar with royalty, power, and the underworld. Rulers took jaguar names, wore jaguar pelts, and sat on jaguar-decorated thrones.

Among the Aztecs, elite warriors were known as jaguar warriors, a military order that dressed in spotted skins and fought as symbols of strength and ferocity. Across the Amazon, shamans have long described transformations between human and jaguar, using the animal as a bridge between the visible world and the spiritual one.

This wasn't decoration. It was recognition. Human beings looked at an animal that owned the night, walked between land and water, and moved through the forest without being seen, and concluded that it must belong to a different order of existence.

Honestly? They weren't wrong.

DO THEY ATTACK PEOPLE?

Rarely. And that fact is one of the most misunderstood in wildlife biology.

Despite its power, the jaguar is generally shy of humans. Confirmed attacks on people in the wild are unusual, especially compared to the sheer number of overlapping habitats. The animal has every physical tool required to hurt a person, and it very seldom uses them that way.

Why? Probably because we aren't part of its normal diet, and a predator that lives by careful energy calculations rarely starts fights it doesn't need. Most encounters end with the cat simply leaving.

That's not an invitation. It's not a promise. Wild predators are wild predators, and unpredictable behavior always exists. But the popular image of the jaguar as a man-eater has always been more myth than statistic.

The truth is stranger: the most dangerous animal in the forest spends most of its energy making sure you never even see it.

THE FIRST 100 DAYS

Every apex predator starts as something helpless.

After a gestation of roughly three months, a female jaguar gives birth to a small litter, usually one to four cubs. They arrive blind, tiny, and completely dependent, born in a hidden den in dense cover or a cave to keep them safe from anything that might see them as prey. Yes, even other predators.

The mother raises them alone. She hunts, returns, defends, moves the den if needed, and teaches them everything over the next year and a half or more: how to stalk, how to read wind and shadow, where the safe crossings are, how to bite where it counts.

Many cubs don't survive. The wild has no guarantee for anyone, not even future kings.

The animal you're looking at is a survivor of a very long series of very unlikely events. Every adult jaguar is a statistical miracle with claws.

THE THING PEOPLE ALWAYS GET WRONG ABOUT ANIMALS LIKE THIS

Whenever a video with a big cat goes viral, the same debate erupts. Half the comments say "so cute." The other half say "so dangerous." Both are missing the point.

A jaguar isn't a pet. It isn't a monster. It's an exceptionally refined predator whose behavior is the sum of instincts, learning, environment, and individual temperament, and every individual is different.

Big cats in professional care, such as accredited sanctuaries, zoos, and rehabilitation centers, live under very specific protocols, trained staff, and safety systems built from decades of hard lessons. Those environments exist for a reason, and they are not something to imitate.

The right response to seeing a moment like this is awe, not imitation. Respect the distance. Respect the muscle. Respect the fact that the calm you're watching is a product of context, trust, and expertise you can't see in the frame.

Wonder is good. Recklessness is how animals and people both end up hurt.

THE STAT THAT SHOULD KEEP YOU UP TONIGHT

Let me give you the number that reframes everything.

Somewhere in a forest right now, an animal is walking silently along a riverbank. It weighs as much as a grown man. It can crack shells and skulls. It can swim a river, climb a tree, and vanish into shadow while standing in plain view. It carries a coat that no other living creature shares, a coat that took millions of years to design.

And it's rare. Rarer than you think. Rarer than most people know.

You are living in a window of history where you can still watch this animal on a phone screen and know that it still exists in the wild. That window is not guaranteed. Every species that disappeared once looked, to the people alive at the time, as though it would always be there.

Attention is the first form of protection. You cannot defend what you never noticed.

THE TONGUE, THE TEETH, THE TOOLKIT

One more detail most people never think about.

Cat tongues are covered in tiny backward-facing barbs made of keratin, the same protein as your fingernails. On a house cat they feel like sandpaper. On a big cat, that surface is a working tool: it scrapes meat from bone, cleans fur, and grooms a coat that has to stay in perfect condition to keep doing its camouflage job.

Add long canines for gripping and killing, carnassial teeth that slice like shears, and claws that retract to stay sharp until the exact moment they're needed.

Every piece of the body is a specialized instrument. Nothing is random. Nothing is wasted.

NOW GO BACK AND WATCH IT AGAIN

Scroll up. Hit replay.

This time, ignore everything you first noticed. Watch the way the pattern moves. Watch how much power is held in check. Watch how something built for one kind of violence can also carry itself with total, unhurried calm.

Then remember what you just read: the bite, the rosettes, the ancient names, the rivers, the sea turtle beaches, the 173,000 that remain, and the enormous machinery of nature standing behind one single frame of animal.

You'll see it differently now. That's what knowledge does. It turns a pretty video into a window.

If this changed how you look at big cats, do three things:

Repost this so more people learn the real story. Follow for more deep dives into the strangest, smartest, most extreme animals on Earth. Reply with the animal you want broken down next. The wilder, the better.
Because the natural world is the greatest story ever told, and most people are scrolling right past it.
Not you. Not anymore.

P.S. Save this post. In a year, when someone asks you why the jaguar matters, you'll be the only person in the room who actually knows. Send it to a friend who thinks a jaguar is just a big spotted cat.

text:
$BTC Update:

In my last update, I was bullish on   from $64K. I wasn't expecting $72K to arrive that quickly, but once the weekly candle closed above $72.8K, I continued holding my spot bag.
At the peak, I was up over 35% on my invested amount.
Now, BTC is approaching another major resistance zone: $86.1K–$88.8K.
These aren't random levels. This zone aligns with the 0.5 Fibonacci retracement, measured from the August 2024 low to the October 2026 ATH, as well as the upper bands of the Anchored VWAP from the previous cycle's 2022 ATL.
Those VWAP bands have acted as support and resistance multiple times historically. BTC also bounced perfectly from the main VWAP earlier this year. The confluence here is worth paying attention to.

BTC's Current Range

BTC is trading within a relatively tight range, with $82.2K–$88.8K defining the boundaries.
Here's what I'm watching:
Weekly close above $88.7K: Opens up the next range at $91K–$93.4K.
Weekly close below $82K: Opens up the $78.6K–$74K zone.
The lower zone has some interesting confluence of its own. It aligns with the 0.618 Fibonacci retracement, the September low, and the 200-day EMA.
For now, these are the two levels that matter most to me. A move outside the range is one thing; a confirmed weekly close is what I'm looking for.

The CLARITY Act failed. The Fed delivered a 25 bps hike for the first time since 2023.
Bitcoin pumped anyway.
When bearish news stops pushing price lower, it usually tells us something. Either the move is being driven by mechanical positioning, or underlying demand is starting to absorb the selling.
In this case, I think it was a combination of both: a short squeeze and genuine spot buying.
Why I don't think this was purely leverage-driven:
Open interest didn't explode alongside price.
In a leverage-driven rally, you'd generally expect OI and price to expand together as new positions enter the market. Here, BTC rallied while OI remained relatively flat.
That's consistent with shorts closing rather than a wave of new longs opening.
The $2B+ in ETF inflows over four consecutive days also supported the spot-demand side of the move.
The rally had structural support. It wasn't simply a case of leverage pushing price higher.

The Macro Picture Hasn't Improved
The September hike itself wasn't a surprise. Markets were pricing in a 93%+ probability ahead of the meeting.
Nothing unexpected happened. The dip before the decision and the recovery afterward were a classic sell-the-rumor, buy-the-fact reaction. But here's the important part: the broader macro situation has not improved.
10Y yield: 5.22%
30Y yield: 5.44% — a 19-year high
DXY: Above 101
Oil: Still elevated
Probability of another hike on October 27: Around 70%
The market got its relief, but the underlying macro pressures remain. And this is where I think many people could get caught off guard.
The short squeeze is now over. That mechanical upward pressure was a one-time event. BTC needs genuine new buyers to sustain the move, hold above $82,281, and push higher.
Without that demand, the rally becomes much more vulnerable.

PCE and NFP: The Next Major Tests

The next two events I'm watching are:
September 30: PCE
October 2: NFP
These could significantly change rate expectations and, consequently, the outlook for risk assets.
If the data comes in softer:
Hike probability could fall from around 70% toward 50–60%.
That would give markets some short-term relief, potentially allowing BTC to extend its rally.
If the data comes in hotter:
Hike probability could move above 85%, making an October hike much more likely. That would keep pressure on risk assets.
But there's a bigger point here that I think deserves attention.

Why the Surprise Matters More Than the Decision
The most dangerous outcome for Bitcoin isn't necessarily a hike with an 85% probability.
It's a hike when the market is sitting at 50/50.
Market reactions are driven by the difference between expectations and reality, not simply by the event itself.
If a hike is already priced in at 85%+, the actual decision may be largely absorbed.
But if the market assigns a 50% probability to a hike and it happens, that's a genuine hawkish surprise.
That's when the risk of a much sharper reaction increases.
The opposite is equally true. If the market is pricing a 50/50 outcome and the Fed pauses, that creates a meaningful dovish surprise.
At the current 70% hike probability, a pause would actually be the more unexpected outcome.
That asymmetry matters when looking at market positioning.

The Fed's Language Matters Too

The actual decision isn't the only thing that matters. The statement and press conference can change the market's interpretation entirely.
A hike accompanied by language suggesting that this is likely the final hike of the cycle could be interpreted as net bullish.
A pause accompanied by a warning that the Fed remains prepared to act in December could be interpreted as net bearish.
You can get the direction of the rate decision right and still get the market reaction wrong.
The forward guidance matters just as much as the headline.
US–Iran ceasefire probability is currently around 60% on prediction markets.
A confirmed ceasefire could push Brent below $90 before the PCE or NFP data even comes out.
That would potentially change the forward inflation outlook and reduce expectations for an October hike.
Under that scenario, hike probability could fall from around 70% toward 40–45%, driven by geopolitical developments rather than economic data.
That would be a significant shift in the macro picture, and BTC could react sharply.
Of course, a prediction-market probability isn't confirmation of an actual ceasefire. This remains a potential catalyst, not an established outcome.

Has the Bitcoin Cycle Bottom Already Formed?

It's difficult to say with confidence.
Several popular Bitcoin bottom indicators are already showing conditions historically associated with cycle lows.
Here's what I'm watching:
1. Bitcoin MVRV Ratio
Bitcoin has historically formed major bottoms when the MVRV ratio falls below 1.
This time, however, BTC rallied more than 35% after the MVRV ratio reached approximately 1.21.
The market didn't need to reach the historical threshold before recovering.
2. Bitcoin Ahr999 Index
The Ahr999 Index falling below 1 is traditionally viewed as a potential bottom-buying zone.
3. Bitcoin Rainbow Chart
The Rainbow Chart is currently showing the FIRE SALE! zone.
4. Previous Cycle High
Bitcoin has historically shown a tendency to form cycle bottoms near the previous cycle's all-time high.
5. Hash Ribbons
This is one of the indicators I personally use when looking for potential cycle bottoms.
So far, it hasn't given a buy signal.
6. Pitchfork
BTC has also bounced from the median line of my Pitchfork.
Taken together, these indicators suggest that BTC could be approaching or may already have established a major bottom. But none of them can confirm that the cycle low is definitively in.
Personally, I think the probability of BTC making a new low this year is extremely low. I also see an extremely low probability of BTC closing the yearly candle above $100K. I'd put both scenarios close to zero.
That's my current view, not a certainty.

Positioning at a good price matters more to me than trying to buy the exact bottom. Trying to catch the absolute low is largely a guessing game. I'd rather build a position around levels that offer a reasonable risk-to-reward profile than sit around waiting for the perfect entry.

What Am I Expecting Next?
My current expectation is that BTC could revisit levels below $79K.
If that happens, I'm planning to look for opportunities to buy spot or open new long positions around these regions:
$76K
$73K
$67K

I'm also expecting a sharp pullback if BTC reaches the $88.7K or $93K region. That doesn't mean the market has to follow this exact path. These are the areas where I'd be paying attention.

I'm definitely not interested in opening fresh swing longs with bigger amount of margin at current levels, especially with the Fear & Greed Index sitting at 74. If BTC reaches $88.7K without a meaningful pullback, I expect the index could push above 80, into Extreme Greed. That's not the environment where I want to chase price. DXY is also approaching a major breakout zone, while USDT.D is nearing an area where it could bounce. Both are worth watching before taking on additional long exposure.

Can BTC Hit $88K+ Before $78.8K?
Yes.
That's entirely possible.

I'm not certain which level will be reached first and I'm not going to pretend otherwise. BTC could continue higher from here or we could see a pullback before the next leg up.

text:
GTA 6 Gameinformer interview:

- World & Map Scale: Set in Leonida, Rockstar’s largest map to date is roughly double the size of GTA V’s, featuring higher density, deeper interactivity, and expanded interior spaces. Key areas include Vice City, the Leonida Keys, Grassrivers, Port Gellhorn, Ambrosia, and Mount Kalaga National Park, alongside swamps, beaches, and rural landscapes. Activities range from ATV trails and mud parks to mountain biking, golf, and bass fishing (though Orlando and the Space Coast remain unconfirmed).

- Protagonists & Dynamic Relationship: Players can seamlessly switch between Jason and Lucia during free roam and missions as they navigate the fallout of a failed heist. Their dynamic—whether strictly platonic or romantic—is shaped by player choices and subtle interactions like holding hands or staying in touch. While neither relationship path offers gameplay buffs, your decisions actively influence the narrative trajectory.

- Heists, Law Enforcement, & Crime: Missions allow for solo or co-op approaches, either stealthy or loud, with income impacting mission progression. A 6-star Wanted Level returns alongside a new "Heat" mechanic and realistic police tracking based on appearance and location. Players can shake the cops by swapping clothes, changing hairstyles, or switching getaway cars. Getting caught as either character triggers a "Busted" sequence.

- Vehicle Theft & Tech: High-end cars feature active alarm systems and GPS trackers. Players must use specialized tools to hotwire them and can utilize the in-game WAiNK app to scan vehicles for security risks, resale values, and registration costs.

- Navigation & Social Features: The map sports a satellite layout, and fast travel is handled via the RydeMe ride-share app, where you can ride alongside other passengers. While Jason and Lucia can browse in-game social media and listen to new licensed music on the radio, their wanted status prevents them from posting content.

- Dynamic Weather & Ecosystems: Weather operates localized systems—storms can brew nearby while your immediate area remains sunny. Persistent effects include standing rainwater, dynamic rainbows, and wind physics applied to vegetation, water, and character hair. Major extreme weather events like tropical storms and hurricanes are officially confirmed.

- Wildlife & Tracking: Over 170 animal species inhabit Leonida, including 60+ bird types and 30+ land mammals. Featured wildlife includes alligators, manatees, sharks, whales, and invasive species like iguanas and macaques. Players can hunt and track animals categorized into Rare, Discoverable, and Legendary tiers.

- Minigames & NPC Realism: Side activities include Base jumping, kayaking, scuba diving, street racing, jet skiing, gyms, billiards, and mini-golf. Crowds feature significantly varied body types, skin textures, tattoos, and attire, backed by dedicated dialogue writing for ambient NPC interactions.

- Supporting Cast: Confirmed characters include Cal Hampton, Dre'Quan Priest, Raul Bautista, Boobie Ike, Brian Heder (voiced by Stephen Root), and the rap duo Real Dimez.

text:
My perspective is that we are going to see a meaningful level of consolidation/ concentration as many retiring owners close shop. But this requires somebody else to pick up that work as it won’t simply disappear. This is where there is a big opportunity for smaller operations to grow. 

I don’t think headcount is going to be a meaningful metric though, revenue per employee will be the more meaningful signal. 

Adopting customer-facing technology will be key to make it as easy as possibly for customers to buy from you. Adopting technology that automated key production activities will be key to increasing output volumes and speeds with lower headcount than today. Simultaneously, it will help drive down production costs and allow those businesses to offer more competitive pricing to customers. Improved pricing, combined with higher quality results and faster production turnaround times will drive more businesses.

This of course, will necessitate continued investment and a willingness/ desire to grow by these businesses, which is MUCH easier said than done. 

I also think, particularly in the case of tool & die shops, there is a real potential for us to see meaningful demand growth. As companies you supply adopt the operational technology/ automation improvements to increase their output, they will require more from their tool and die suppliers.

With that said, some may try to bring it in house since everyone loves to cry “VERTICAL INTEGRATION BABAYYYY” which is a whole other conversation. But, that kinda gets to the point of why you want to grow and diversify your customer base so no single account makes up a material percentage of your business. 

At the end of the day, as work consolidates/ concentrates in the coming decades, I think the companies that win are the ones that deliver:
 
1) a simple/ seamless customer experience
2) competitive prices w/ strong margins from tech/ automation
3) consistently high quality work
4) quick turnaround on work
5) transparency/ good communication throughout the process

Oh Naa Sidhayya’ Team Organises Grand Job Fair in Hi-Tech City
Entertainment Meets Social Responsibility with 1,000+ Job Opportunities

Hyderabad, September 29, 2026: The team of the private song ‘Oh Naa Sidhayya’, featuring Katyayani Jagan as Chittemma and Siddu Reddy Kandakattla as Sidhayya, organised a grand job fair at Cyber Gardens, Jubilee Enclave, near Shilparamam, Hi-Tech City, with the aim of combining entertainment with meaningful social responsibility.

The event was organised under the leadership of the cast and crew, including Siddu Reddy Kandakattla, Director Ramu and DOP Arun. The initiative reflects Siddu Reddy Kandakattla’s vision of extending his activities beyond entertainment by supporting employment generation, social welfare and community development.

70+ IT and Non-IT Companies Participate

More than 70 IT and non-IT companies participated in the job fair, offering over 1,000 employment opportunities to job seekers. Candidates had the opportunity to interact directly with company representatives, attend interviews and, where eligible, receive spot offer letters.

Leading organisations including TCS, Sagility, Teleperformance, HGS, Tata Motors, Tech Mahindra, Digitide, Genpact, Justdial, Reliance Digital, Axis Bank, IDBI Bank and Neon Motors, among others, participated in the recruitment drive.

Job opportunities were available across multiple sectors, including IT, software, banking, logistics, automobiles, pharmaceuticals, nursing, marketing, digital marketing, hospitality, sales, driving, engineering, accounts, and voice and non-voice processes.

Candidates with qualifications ranging from 10th standard, Intermediate, ITI and Diploma to https://t.co/qHByvZH2cN, B.Pharm, M.Pharm, https://t.co/bQeqMknxra, MBA and other degree qualifications participated. Both freshers and experienced professionals attended the job fair.

Health Insurance Support for 300 Auto Drivers

As part of the team’s social responsibility initiatives, health insurance coverage of ₹3 lakh each was extended to 300 auto drivers and their families. According to the organisers, the coverage can be utilised for various medical needs. They also stated that financial assistance of up to ₹10.50 lakh would be provided in the event of an unforeseen incident, subject to applicable terms and conditions.

The organisers said the initiative reflects their commitment to providing meaningful support to different sections of society.

Insurance Support for Technical Crew

The team has also undertaken an initiative to provide insurance support to members of the direction, camera and other technical departments who contributed to the making of ‘Oh Naa Sidhayya’.

text:
A ‘Twilight Consciousness’ May Exist in Dying Patients, Scientists Say. Could That Mean Death Isn’t Final?
Just before it ceases functioning, the brain may make a last-ditch effort to find unresolved purpose or a reason to stay alive 
The article’s “twilight consciousness” idea refers to the possibility that some brain activity may continue briefly during the process of dying. In a few monitored cases, researchers have observed bursts of high-frequency gamma activity around cardiac arrest or severe oxygen loss. Gamma waves are associated with processes such as perception and memory in a functioning brain, but their presence alone does not prove that a person is conscious, having meaningful experiences, or able to recover. The evidence is limited, and scientists still debate what these signals mean.
Near-death experiences—such as vivid memories, a sense of leaving the body, or encounters with loved ones—are sometimes offered as clues that the brain may remain active during a crisis. One proposed explanation is that extreme stress, disrupted oxygen supply, and changes in brain chemistry can produce intense, dream-like experiences. Other explanations are being studied, and current research cannot establish that consciousness continues after the brain has irreversibly stopped functioning.
The article also raises an important distinction: cardiac arrest is not the same as brain death. Cardiac arrest may sometimes be reversed with resuscitation; brain death, when properly diagnosed under accepted medical standards, is the irreversible loss of all brain function. Rare reports of movement or reflexes in critically ill patients require careful medical assessment, but they do not by themselves show awareness or invalidate brain-death criteria.
Overall, “twilight consciousness” is a research question—not evidence that death is not final. Organ donation decisions rely on established safeguards, including formal determination of death and strict clinical protocols. These findings may encourage further research and careful communication, but they do not currently change the medical definition of death.

text:
35-year-old Aileen Wuornos was awaiting trial in Florida when a stranger saw her story on the news and decided to write to her. That stranger was Arlene Pralle, a horse breeder from Ocala who said she felt spiritually called to offer Wuornos the kind of maternal relationship she believed had been missing from her life.

By then, Wuornos had been arrested in connection with the deaths of several men in central Florida between 1989 and 1990. Investigators had linked her to the cases through evidence including pawn records, fingerprints, property belonging to victims and statements she made after her arrest. Her former partner, Tyria Moore, also cooperated with authorities and helped investigators obtain a recorded confession.

Pralle began corresponding with Wuornos while she was in jail in 1991. The relationship quickly became much more than an exchange of letters. In November of that year, Arlene and her husband, Robert Pralle, legally adopted the 35-year-old Wuornos as their adult daughter.

The adoption placed the couple directly inside one of the most closely watched criminal cases in the country. Arlene became a vocal supporter of Wuornos, publicly defending her and helping manage attention surrounding the case. The Pralles also became involved with her legal team as Wuornos prepared to face trial.

In 1992, Wuornos was convicted in the death of Richard Mallory and received a death sentence. She later entered guilty or no-contest pleas in five additional cases, ultimately receiving six death sentences.

Over the years, Wuornos changed her account of what happened. She initially maintained that she acted in self-defense, but later withdrew that claim and eventually stopped pursuing appeals. She was executed by the State of Florida on October 9, 2002.

Before the trials, convictions and years of appeals, however, came an unexpected relationship: a woman watching the news saw a jailed stranger and decided not only to contact her, but to legally make her part of the family.

text:
An Interview With Lee Kuan Yew 2008

Q: How do you see Iraq?

Lee: "I don't know what happened to Dick Cheney. He allowed himself to believe with Richard Perle and the neocons you could change Iraq. How could you change Iraq, a 4,000-year-old society that is not malleable? Everybody knows the troubles the British had during and after World War I. Ideology should have no place when making geopolitical assessments."

Q: In fact, democracies don't produce great statesmen anymore. Why?

Lee: "You now have, and I don't know how long this phase will last, mass media domination, owned by a group of media barons who want constant change for their balance sheets.

It depends on the nature of the crisis that must be faced. When a real crisis sets in, a matter of life and death, opinion formulators realize this is no time to be pontificating, but a time to stay the course with someone who understands what this is all about. Short of that, the media help put a leader on the pedestal and then start chopping away at the pedestal until he/she falls in disgrace. That's part of the cycle of constant change. Watch Sarkozy in France. They hoisted him up to prominence and now they're already attempting to bring him down through his personal life

But it's also the enormous pressure of media competition and the giant appetite for advertising revenue, what television program gets what viewership, or eyeballs, or clicks online. Never mind the consequences. If you get the advertising, you win."

Q:  As I travel in moderate Muslim states in North Africa, the Middle East and South Asia, I ask heads of state and government how many extremists, or would-be jihadis, they estimate live in their midst, also how many fundamentalists who support openly or secretly the jihadi cause. The answer is usually 1 percent and 10 percent. In a country like Pakistan, that translates to 1.6 million extremists and 16 million supporters. On a global scale, that comes out to roughly 14 million extremists and 140 million sympathizers

Lee: "Yes, but I do not see them winning, and by that I mean able to impose their extremist system. I can see them inducing fear and insecurity, and causing fear, but they don't have the technology and the organization to overwhelm any government."

Q: So we're doing the right thing?

Lee: "No. Iraq was a mistake. I've said this before and I said this in the presence of Paul Wolfowitz, one of the architects of the invasion, at an IISS conference two months after the fall of Saddam Hussein, when someone asked me what will happen in Iraq. In October 2002, I was in Washington and became quite convinced an invasion would take place. On the way home, I stopped in London and asked Tony Blair to brief me. After 45 minutes, I said, "Look I accept the argument that with British and American military capabilities it would be a walk over, but then what do you do the day after? Blair replied, "That's up to the Americans." I then said to Blair, "If you were in charge, what would you do?" His political adviser then stepped in and said, "We would appoint the strongest pro-Western general and then get out quickly." So I repeated all that at the IISS conference and explained this reflected the institutional memory of what the British had been through in Iraq in the early 1920s. Paul Wolfowitz stood up in high dudgeon. So to placate him, I said, "Of course the British don't have the resources you have."

Q: Did Wolfowitz ask anything of you?

Lee: "Yes, he came to my office to ask that Singapore send police trainers to Iraq. I had known Paul since his days as an ambassador at the State Department. I said, "Paul, do you realize how long it takes to train a policeman in Singapore? And that's only in one language, English, and it still takes two years. And you want me to teach Iraqis how to do it in three months in English? No, he replied, we'll supply translators. This is an emergency, he said, and many nations are helping us. So I replied OK, but we'll do it in Amman, Jordan, not Baghdad, where we would become the targets of suicide bombers. When he told me they had disbanded Saddam's police force, I became very nervous. Because when the Japanese came down here in World War II, 20,000 of their troops captured 90,000 British, Indian and Australian troops. They sent them into captivity, but they left the local police in charge, and kept all the other positions of the British administration intact — from power management to the gas board — and simply put Japanese in charge of each British position. And 20,000 Japanese troops moved on to Java. But in Iraq, you disbanded everything, and tried to run things without the former Baath party officials who had been in charge of civil administration. You created an ungovernable vacuum."

Q: Why do you think this was so?

Lee: "From Day One, the idea of remaking Iraq, without the civil service in place and without recalling Saddam's army to service, showed a frightening lack of understanding of local conditions and elementary facts of political and economic life in Iraq. In ancient days, those who invaded and conquered China on horseback got off their horses and applied themselves to the more difficult job of governing."

Q: So you do feel that NATO's future is at stake in Afghanistan?

A: No doubt about it. But you should also realize Afghanistan cannot succeed as a democracy. You attempted too much. Let the warlords sort it out in such a way you don't try to build a new state. The British tried it and failed. Just make clear if they commit aggression again and offer safe haven to Taliban, they will be punished.

Q: In the next 12 months, China, in this New Year of the Rat (Feb. 7) that you are now celebrating, will mark its transformation in the past three decades from one of the poorest countries in the 20th century into the world's third-largest economy, soon to displace Germany, as the globe's new engine room of economic growth. Will China be to the 21st century what America was to the 20th?

A: The Chinese leadership has come to the conclusion if they stay on their present course, the peaceful rise of China's power will prevail. They are determined not to challenge any existing power, meaning America, EU, Russia, but just make friends with everybody. Given the rules of the game now that China is in WTO, they can only grow stronger year by year, and within three or four decades, China's GDP will be equal to America's, their technology will be equal to what was long regarded as the world's only superpower, and their GDP will be larger than America's. And all that stems from what they have long studied in detail in Taiwan, Hong Kong and Singapore. When Deng Xiaoping came to Singapore he was amazed at what he saw, as his briefing papers did not tally with his own eyes. That's when he must have concluded the Communist system didn't work. He could see how we were exploiting Western capitalism and had plants all over the place with cheaper labor and exporting goods all over the world. Hell's bells, he said, we can do that, too. That's when China began setting up special economic zones around coastal cities. They saw Hong Kong, Taiwan and Singapore with the advantages of close ties with the West, access to Western technology, export markets, knowledge, capital and an educated workforce. Now with WTO, they are on the same course, sending 250,000 students abroad every year, and even though they may lose 60 percent to 70 percent of them to other countries, they don't care because they know many of them will come back eventually. Year by year, they're closing the gap.

Q: And all this peacefully?

A: I watched "The Rise of the Great Powers" and I was amazed at this scholarly job by noted historians. No Communist or leftist jargon. How did some of these powers rise in history? Tiny little Portugal? Naval technology, pure and simple. Christopher Columbus? Spain? Tiny Holland, the French, the British, the armada, what was the trick? Technology plus governments that united the people in a common objective toward growth.

I was quite surprised when this television program analyzed the British rise to global power status. The barons brought the king to Magna Carta, and said you will rule through us, Parliament, not divine right, but divine right through us. And when the king misbehaved, such as Charles I, he was beheaded. It was subversive to advocate cutting off the head of the Communist Party, but in today's China the people have confidence in the leaders because they allowed the once-hated merchant class to emerge and grow. That's the same dynamics that once created the East India Company and created an empire.

Q: So you see China on the same glide path?

A: I think so. But they want to avoid building a pre-World War II Japan or a Germany. Territorial conquest is not necessary as it once was. You don't have to be a genius to know that they are producing five times as many engineers and scientists as the Americans. What is it they need most now? Roads, railways, infrastructure. They are everywhere in Africa, in the Arab world, Latin America. China is everywhere today. Can you be everywhere while focused on Iraq? In the Caribbean you have one embassy in Barbados that serves six other tiny island countries. The Chinese have an embassy in each place. And that's what you call your front yard.

Q: Are you saying this will be China's century?

A: They will want to share this century as co-equals. By 2030, it will be a different world. They won't invade Taiwan and try to take over militarily. That would be far too costly for them all over the world. The U.S. Pacific commander said, "Look, you've got all these forces trained to knock off our 7th Fleet and if Taiwan declares its independence you will have to move. I would be quite happy to leave it as it is, but not Beijing." In my opinion, Chinese leaders would also be happy to leave it as it is. Taiwan goes to America to get its technology, which then transits to China. If they take back Taiwan, it becomes Chinese without the same freedom of access to U.S. technology and research labs. So why kill the goose that lays the golden eggs? The Chinese are quite comfortable leaving Taiwan the way it is.

Q: How many top brains do you consider lost to Singapore every year?

A: At the top end, about 1,000 a year. That's a loss of 4 percent or 5 percent. But compensating that, we have Chinese and Indians coming here looking for better prospects. So on balance, we're still gainers. But the day will come when China, in 30 or 40 years, will offer better prospects than any country in the world.

Q: So to conclude, back to what concerns you most about the next 10 years, including WMD terrorism?

A: First whether America will face this next rough patch without losing heart. Afghanistan cannot succeed as a democracy, nor as a new state defying centuries of tradition. To remake societies is beyond the capacity of any nation. America as a superpower has global responsibilities — but that's not one of them. Utopias have no place in geopolitics.

Ipe Alternatives for Texas Lake Homes: Why Composite Decking Outperforms Traditional Wood by US Lumber Brokers https://t.co/XrbqfN5TeG 
Ipe Alternatives for Texas Lake Homes: Why Composite Decking Outperforms Traditional Wood
📷US Lumber BrokersFollowingSep 20, 20269 min read·
Press enter or click to view image in full size📷The Challenge: Ipe Scarcity and Cost for Lakeside Texas Homes
Texas lake homes demand decking materials that can handle intense sun, humidity swings, and water exposure without compromising the warm, expressive aesthetic that defines contemporary architecture. Yet sourcing Ipe continues to challenge architects and builders alike. Limited supply chains, escalating costs, and sustainability concerns push many of our clients toward alternatives that deliver comparable or superior performance.We’ve spent years sourcing premium deck materials for lakeside projects across Texas. This article covers the realistic alternatives to Ipe, explains why each performs differently in Texas environments, and guides you toward the material that best serves your specific design intent.Ipe hardwood has long been the benchmark for tropical decking: dense, rot-resistant, and naturally fire-resistant. But sourcing it reliably has become increasingly difficult. Import delays, inconsistent inventory, and price volatility now define the Ipe market. A premium deck project that relied on Ipe five years ago might face 16–20 week lead times today, alongside price premiums that can add $40,000 to $80,000 to a mid-sized lakeside deck.For architects designing homes around Lake Travis, Lake Austin, or Hill Country waterfront properties, these constraints force hard conversations early in the specification phase. Clients expect premium materials without premium wait times. That tension created an opportunity for us to develop genuinely competitive alternatives rather than compromise on durability or aesthetics.The real problem isn’t that Ipe works poorly. It’s that Ipe no longer represents the most practical path to achieving the design goals your clients expect.Why Architects Demand Premium Deck Solutions
Modern residential architecture in Texas prizes honest material expression. A deck isn’t merely functional infrastructure; it’s an extension of the home’s living narrative. Architects like those inspired by Lake|Flato understand that wood cladding, decking, and structural elements communicate warmth, permanence, and connection to place.Lakeside environments amplify these demands. Water reflection intensifies UV exposure. Humidity cycles stress material stability. Freeze-thaw cycles (rare but real during Hill Country winters) test structural integrity. Performance failures on a deck don’t just disappoint clients; they undermine the architect’s vision and the builder’s reputation.Premium solutions must deliver four commitments simultaneously:Visual authenticity that photographs well and ages gracefully
Structural reliability across Texas climate variables
Minimal maintenance burden for homeowners
Defensible sustainability credentials
Ipe delivers on points one and two historically. Points three and four have always been compromises. Modern alternatives now outperform Ipe on several of these criteria.Understanding Ipe: The Tropical Hardwood Standard
Ipe (pronounced ee-pay) is a Brazilian hardwood so dense it sinks in water. Its natural oil content resists rot, insects, and UV damage. Builders can specify it without finish, confident it will weather to an elegant silver-gray patina over 15–20 years. That durability justifies its cost in high-stakes projects.But durability alone doesn’t define performance. Ipe’s density makes it difficult to machine. Fastening requires pre-drilling. Installation costs run 20–30% higher than softer alternatives. The material also moves minimally with moisture, which can create gaps if seasonal humidity varies significantly. In Texas lakeside environments, those gaps collect debris and water.Most importantly, Ipe sourcing now involves ethical complexity. While legally harvested Ipe exists, traceability remains inconsistent. Architects committed to sustainability increasingly hesitate to specify it, even when clients expect premium tropical hardwood aesthetics.Our Comprehensive Alternative Solutions: Beyond Single-Product Comparisons
We don’t advocate for one-size-fits-all material selection. Instead, we match material properties to project conditions and design intent. A Hill Country home with southern sun exposure demands different performance characteristics than a shaded lakeside cabin or an open deck facing north across water.Our solution suite includes:Thermally modified softwoods for architects who prioritize authentic wood appearance and hand-craftable details
Composite engineering for maximum durability in high-moisture zones with minimal visible maintenance
Hardwood alternatives (Cumaru, Garapa, Tigerwood) for tropical aesthetics without Ipe’s sourcing burden
WUI Class A fire-rated products for Hill Country properties where fire risk justifies premium specification
Each pathway delivers different value. Understanding which matters most to your project requires honest conversation about climate exposure, design priorities, and ownership expectations.Thermally Modified Wood: Sustainable Performance Meets Design Intent
Thermally modified wood decking represents a genuine innovation for architects seeking authentic wood character without Ipe’s complexity. The process heats domestic softwoods (Pine, Ash, Poplar) to specific temperatures in oxygen-free environments, chemically altering the wood’s cell structure.The result: a material that behaves like hardwood despite softwood origins. It resists rot, dimensions more stably, and accepts stain beautifully. Lead times collapse because we source domestic inventory. Cost runs 40–50% below Ipe. And the sustainability story is compelling: we’re enhancing abundant domestic resources rather than relying on tropical imports.Thermally modified wood does have limits. It’s softer than Ipe, so foot traffic can create surface distress over time. But for architects prioritizing hand-crafted details and warm wood tones, that subtle patina actually enhances the design narrative. The material also machines beautifully, allowing fluted profiles, custom soffits, and bespoke details that would be impractical with Ipe.For a 2,000 square-foot deck in the Hill Country, thermally modified ash can save $25,000 compared to Ipe while delivering superior sustainability credentials.Composite Decking Technology: Engineering Durability for Texas Water Exposure
Composite decking merges wood fibers with polymer matrices to eliminate the maintenance burden that comes with authentic wood. We source leading brands including TimberTech, Trex, and Fiberon specifically because their engineering evolves constantly.Modern composites look nothing like the plasticky alternatives from 15 years ago. High-quality options now offer wood grain fidelity that satisfies most architectural specifications. The real advantage, though, lies in performance consistency. No checking. No cupping. No seasonal movement. In a high-humidity lakeside environment, that stability prevents the small failures that accumulate into major problems.Composites also dominate in low-maintenance zones. A deck facing direct sun with southern exposure needs cleaning every two years. Composite decking requires light brushing and occasional soap washing. Most homeowners accept this trade-off enthusiastically.The aesthetic compromise is real, however. Composite materials don’t patina like wood. They don’t develop character with age. For architects committed to authentic wood expression, composites represent pragmatism rather than inspiration. But for clients who view decks as functional living space first and aesthetic statement second, composites often outperform expectations.WUI Class A Fire-Rated Options for Hill Country Properties
Hill Country properties deserve special attention. Wildfire risk has transformed from theoretical to concrete. WUI Class A fire-rated decking now represents essential specification for properties within zone X or wildland interface areas.We supply multiple WUI-compliant options: thermally modified softwoods, pressure-treated hardwoods, and composite materials engineered to meet Class A standards. Each delivers fire performance while maintaining distinct aesthetic profiles. Some architects specify WUI materials across the entire exterior envelope (decking, cladding, soffits, fascia) for visual consistency.Fire-rated specification adds 10–15% to material cost but transfers significant liability from homeowner to certified material. Insurance companies recognize the distinction, sometimes offering modest premium reductions.Comparing Material Longevity and Maintenance Requirements
A straightforward comparison helps clarify trade-offs:Ipe Hardwood: 20+ year lifespan, virtually no maintenance, but higher installed cost, long lead times, and complex machining. Best for: High-visibility projects where authentic hardwood character justifies premium investment.Thermally Modified Wood: 15–20 year lifespan, light maintenance (occasional sealing), fast availability, and excellent machinability. Best for: Architects designing custom details and homeowners comfortable with subtle wood patina.Composite Decking: 25–30 year lifespan, minimal maintenance (occasional cleaning), predictable performance, and consistent appearance. Best for: High-moisture zones and low-maintenance preferences.Alternative Hardwoods (Cumaru, Garapa): 15–20 year lifespan, minimal maintenance, authentic hardwood character, and better availability than Ipe. Best for: Tropical aesthetic with reasonable lead times.The longevity question isn’t academic. A deck lasting 30 years versus 20 years represents $30,000-$50,000 in avoided replacement cost. That calculation changes material priorities https://t.co/NSQjGDKzam We Source and Supply Premium Alternatives Across Texas

text:
RARE COLOR FOOTAGE: Kingdom of Yugoslavia, 1938 – Sarajevo, Split, Trogir, and the Adriatic Sea
(THIS IS NOT A POLITICAL VIDEO; IT DEPICTS THE CIVILIAN POPULATION AND LANDSCAPES)

These rare color photographs from 1938 portray the Kingdom of Yugoslavia as it was at the time, from vibrant Sarajevo to the port cities and coastal landscapes of the Adriatic. The film opens in Sarajevo with a large parade. Brass bands, units in traditional uniforms, boys and girls dressed uniformly, and numerous civilians march through the streets. Flag bearers wave blue, white, and red Yugoslav flags as well as richly decorated traditional banners. Long shots from different angles immediately convey the scale of the event and the crowds lining the streets.

The camera then turns to everyday life in Sarajevo. Women in traditional dress move through a city adorned with flags, crowds fill the streets, and children eat ice cream. Particularly striking are the detailed color shots of market life. Men wearing fezzes, fully veiled women, merchants, and visitors weave between the stalls. A man in uniform inspects garlic, traders offer their goods, and donkeys carry woven baskets through the lively market. 
Fruit stands, traditional clothing, and the sheer number of people provide a rare and direct glimpse into the daily life of Sarajevo’s Muslim community in 1938.

The second part of the journey takes us to the Adriatic coast. From the moving ship, we first see the small port of Sušak with its fishing boats, waterfront houses, and an old fortress with round towers. 
The voyage continues along the rocky coastline. 

A two‑masted sailing ship with its sails unfurled flies the blue, white, and red Yugoslav flag. In Split, the film captures the atmosphere of the harbor: sailing ships and fishing boats moored at the pier, people moving through the streets, and market stalls offering fruit and vegetables. We also see the Trgovinska Banka, palm‑lined streets, and a wide view of Split and its harbor with the cathedral tower. A steamship enters the port before the journey continues along the coast.

Other scenes show women sitting on sacks on the ground, cracking almonds. The voyage then reaches Trogir. The historic port fortress is visible, as is the Cathedral of St. Lawrence, as the ship passes by. 
The motorboat Najade from Vienna is moored at the Trogir pier. A flag bearing the swastika flies at its stern — a historical detail from 1938.

Finally, the journey continues along the rocky Adriatic coastline. Mountainous hinterlands, port towns, and ancient fortress walls glide past the ship. The ship’s bridge is visible, along with another blue, white, and red Yugoslav flag. The footage conveys extraordinary impressions of public life, traditions, clothing, trade, markets, navigation, and travel in the Kingdom of Yugoslavia — captured in color at a time when most surviving film material is still in black and white.
