With immense respect for their freedom and dignity, the lover simply waits for them to inquire about the love that has filled his or her life.” Last but not least, it is necessary to highlight the persecution suffered by Christians in various parts of the world at the hands of extremist religious groups. Every persecution on religious grounds is always a violation of human dignity, and there is an urgent need to find a common response which, in the spirit of Nostra Aetate, promotes respect, dialogue, and peaceful coexistence among all and toward all.  

DICASTERY FOR THE DOCTRINE OF THE FAITH
DICASTERY FOR PROMOTING CHRISTIAN UNITY
DICASTERY FOR INTERRELIGIOUS DIALOGUE (2026)

https://t.co/ZncNoaN5z1

On the 25th anniversary of 9/11, the Archbishop of Canterbury Sarah Mullally became global meme fodder. Mullally conferred an interfaith award on Osama bin Laden apologist Maulana Hafiz Ashrafi. The photograph went viral. Mullally, an über-feminist who had pledged to wipe out misogyny in the Church, was caught on camera, grinning like a barracuda alongside Ashrafi and his wife, who was dressed like a sarcophagus. Ashrafi’s daughter, masked like a Ninja at a Halloween party, put the finishing touches on the comedy of the absurd. A week later, desperate to compete with his partner in interfaith suicidal empathy, Pope Leo XIV approved a declaration titled “A Journey of Hope” (...) it urges greater dialogue with Hinduism, Buddhism, Jainism, and other religions. It elevates Islam to a key fraternal partner. It castigates perpetrators of “Islamophobia.” It does not preach Jesus’ uniqueness. And it reads the riot act to Christians who engage in the unforgivable sin of “proselytism.” In effect, the declaration is Pope Leo’s ultimatum to St. Paul. “Put your aggressive proselytizing on mute,” Leo is telling Paul. “Cool the sales pitch. Cut the converts. Quit cruising around the Mediterranean persuading Jews and Greeks to follow Jesus. It’s ruining the Vatican’s interreligious dialogue with devotees of Artemis, Zeus, and Hermes and killing our fraternity with disciples of Dionysus, Isis, and Mithras. Leo’s document does not define “proselytism,” leaving room for weaponized ambiguity. Not once does the document use the term “evangelism,” my preferred term for proselytism. One has to turn to the Oxford English Dictionary, which defines “proselytism” as “the making or seeking of converts.” The root word is proserkhesthai, ‘to approach.’ You’ve got to approach someone if you wish to convert them. It is striking that while the Vatican anathematizes proselytism, the European Court of Human Rights approves proselytism as a bona fide manifestation of religion. The ECHR recognized this in the landmark Kokkinakis v Greece case, wherein a Jehovah’s Witness challenged his conviction for attempting to convert a Greek Orthodox Christian on a home visit. Kokkinakis was arrested more than 60 times for proselytism. He was also imprisoned several times. The court based its verdict on the European Convention on Human Rights (Article 9), which asserts that the right to freedom of religion includes the right to change one’s religion (as does Article 18 of the United Nations Universal Declaration of Human Rights). “Proselytism is linked to freedom of religion; a believer must be able to communicate his faith and his beliefs in the religious sphere as in the philosophical sphere,” Judge Pettiti stated. “Believers and agnostic philosophers have a right to expound their beliefs, to try to get other people to share them and even to try to convert those whom they are addressing.” According to the court, proselytism is valid since religious conversion, as permitted by Article 9, often involves being persuaded by others. “Indeed, without proselytism, the right to change religion ‘would be likely to remain a dead letter,’” Andrew Hambler, an expert in employment law, writes in his peer-reviewed article in the Industrial Law Journal. Hambler might as well have quoted the apostle Paul. Writing to the Romans, Paul strings together a series of rhetorical questions: “How then will they call on him [Jesus] in whom they have not believed? And how are they to believe in him of whom they have never heard? And how are they to hear without someone preaching?” (Romans 10:14). In this sense, proselytism has the strongest claim to legitimacy, Hambler emphasizes. Sadly, “proselytism” bashing is now a staple of papal pontificating. During his visit to the Rimini Meeting of Friendships Among Peoples, Leo “recalled that his predecessors have repeated on several occasions, ‘the Church does not engage in proselytism,’” Vatican News reported. In a letter to the cardinals, Leo slammed “the temptation of proselytism.” Pope Francis frequently attacked proselytism. “Proselytism is solemn nonsense; it makes no sense,” he famously said. For Rome, “the view that proselytism is the only way to engage with the other no longer make[s] sense in a world that increasingly resembles an interconnected and constantly evolving global village.” So how does one preach Christ? Sure, Rome isn’t calling for “renouncing the truth” but “proclaiming it in a manner befitting the Gospel: with esteem, listening, and charity.” But the exaggerated emphasis on interreligious dialogue can lead to “grave confusion,” as Bishop Joseph Strickland warns. He contends that Leo’s document risks placing dialogue above evangelization, suggesting that non-Christian religions are authentic paths to God and raising doubts about the Church’s missionary mandate. The New Testament scholar Robert Gagnon observes that Leo’s document “at the very least depresses or discourages evangelism (what it calls ‘proselytism’), if not outright rejecting it.” Gagnon calls the document “utter nonsense,” adding: “It is heretical to discourage conversion to Christianity from other faiths. This Pope and his Vatican cohorts have made many missteps in a relatively short time, but this is the worst.” I would applaud if Leo warned against using coercion, cajolery, or crookery in proselytism. But Leo redefines evangelistic outreach as the supine expectation of a lover whose words “do not disturb others,” do not “make demands or oblige,” but “only lead others to marvel at such love.” Christians must not proactively seek to convert others but, like a lover, “simply wait[s] for them to inquire about the love that has filled his or her life.” This is pious humbug. No great love story would be penned, or no great romantic movie would find an audience if all the lover did was to “simply wait.” Even a peacock proactively opens his feathers and dances to attract a peahen. Jesus didn’t ask his disciples to “simply wait” but to go to the very ends of the earth to proclaim the gospel. Paul did the very opposite of “simply waiting.” He went around the Mediterranean on three missionary journeys. He preached to Jews and Gentiles. Jewish and Christian scholars agree that Paul wasn’t trying to “convert” Jews to “Christianity” or to “Roman Catholicism.” Saul the Jew never became Paul the Christian. He remained a Jew to his death. In the highly fraught sectarian context of Second Temple Judaism, where the Jesus Movement emerged as one of the many Jewish sects, Paul was preaching to the Jews that their Scriptures had been fulfilled and their Jewish Messiah had come in the person of Jesus. Paul is emphatic that the gospel is “to the Jew first.” Much of his preaching takes place in synagogues. The embryonic “churches” are actually synagogue sub-groups comprised of Jewish Jesus followers who keep Torah, Paul Treblico argues in his monograph Self-designations and Group Identity in the New Testament. Paul didn’t “simply wait” for Jews or Gentiles to enquire about Jesus. For example, in the synagogue at Thessalonica, “for three weeks he argued with them from the [Hebrew] scriptures, explaining and proving that it was necessary for the Christ to suffer and to rise from the dead, and saying, ‘This Jesus, whom I proclaim to you, is the Messiah.’” Luke, the author of Acts, notes that “some of them were persuaded” (Acts 17:3-4). The five verbs: arguing, explaining, proving, proclaiming, and persuading, suggest that Paul was proactively proselytizing the Jews. In Athens, Paul “argued” in “the synagogue with the Jews and the devout persons, and in the market place every day with those who chanced to be there” (17:17). Rather than “esteem” other religions, “his spirit was provoked within him as he saw that the city was full of idols” (17:16). The Greek word for “provoked” is paroxyno, from which we get our English word “paroxysm.” In Corinth, he “argued in the synagogue every sabbath and persuaded Jews and Greeks” (18:4). In Ephesus, he “entered the synagogue and for three months spoke boldly, arguing and pleading about the kingdom of God” and “argued daily in the hall of Tyrannus” for two years (19:8-10). Non-Jewish proselytes did indeed attend synagogues. In his magnum opus Jew and Gentile in the Ancient World, Jewish historian Louis Feldman argues that Judaism possessed a robust spirit of proselytism and attracted large numbers of converts and proselytes throughout the Greco-Roman world before the rise of early Christianity. Ironically, while Pope Leo is shying away from proselytism, Islam is making massive inroads with dawa. In July, Muslim organizations launched aggressive proselytization campaigns using the FIFA World Cup series to recruit new converts in 16 cities of the United States, Canada, and Mexico. The Muslim Ummah of North America (MUNA) kicked off its dawa at SoFi Stadium in California with banners inviting football fans to “discover Islam” as a “faith of peace, purpose, and submission to the Creator.” MUNA missionaries offered free copies of the Qur’an in English, Spanish, Bengali, and other languages, promoting the Islamic text as a book that “has inspired billions of people for over 1,400 years” and Islam as a religion “regardless of race, language, nationality, or background.” But scholars and ex-Muslims are warning the West that dawa is not simply the sharing of Islamic faith in the Christian sense of “evangelism.” “Dawa as practiced by radical Islamists employs a wide range of mechanisms to advance their goal of imposing Islamic law (sharia) on society,” Ayaan Hirsi Ali, a human rights activist and former Muslim, explains in her book The Challenge of Dawa: Political Islam as Ideology and Movement and How to Counter It. “The ultimate goal of dawa is to destroy the political institutions of a free society and replace them with the rule of sharialaw.” Like Catholics, many evangelicals are not only failing to understand the sinister aspects of Islamic dawa but, unlike Paul, are unwilling to confront it with robust argumentation and challenge. I find it difficult to comprehend why certain religious groups resent proselytizing others or having their members proselytized. If Jews tried to convert me, I’d feel honoured. In fact, I’d joyfully go with my Jewish proselytizers to the synagogue. Since I read Hebrew, I can join in the prayers. As a chaplain at a London university, I had excellent relations with hardline Muslim leaders. They’d tell me they respect me but loathe my liberal Anglican clergy colleagues. “We know you are trying to convert us and you know we are trying to convert you,” they’d say. In turn, I respected and loved them for their convictions and passion for dawa (Islamic proselytism). My Hindu students were candid: “You’re wasting your time. Britain is a post-Christian country. We are here to convert Britons to Hinduism,” they’d say. On campus, even Buddhists, Stoics, and atheists proselytized unapologetically. It was a playground of ideas. I am richer for my interactions with the evangelists of these religions and philosophies. Likewise, my mission was to preach the gospel and pray that they would come to faith in the Lord Jesus Christ. With Paul, I would remind myself daily: “For I am not ashamed of the gospel, for it is the power of God for salvation to everyone who believes, to the Jew first and also to the Greek” (Romans 1:16). While I was a student in Cambridge, Catholics and Orthodox unrelentingly tried to convert me to their “one, true church.” I felt flattered. A religion that doesn’t proselytize is essentially saying: “We are a closed club. We don’t want you. You are not good enough for us.” On my part, I’ve never missed an opportunity to evangelize. I did this for eight hours while I was flying back from India to England to defend my doctoral thesis, with a Briton who had left Christianity for Buddhism, even though I desperately needed the time to prepare for my viva voce. At the end of our conversation, the Buddhist promised to reconsider the claims of Christ. Leo doesn’t believe in proselytism because he doesn’t understand the transformative power of the gospel. In India, millions of Dalits (untouchables) have been liberated from three millennia of the caste system because missionaries proselytized them. In the Islamic world, millions of Muslims have been unshackled from the slavery of Islam because someone shared Christ with them—as my ex-Muslim colleagues at the Ideological Defense Institute would testify. Paul said: “I’m compelled to do it, and doomed if I don’t!” (1 Corinthians 9:16, The Message). He ends his life and ministry incarcerated in Rome, “expounding the gospel [to his fellow-Jews] from morning till evening, testifying to the kingdom of God and trying to convince them about Jesus both from the law of Moses and from the prophets” (Acts 28:23). In the landmark Mbuyi v Newpark Childcare Ltd employment tribunal case, Sarah Mbuyi, a Christian nursery worker, framed her workplace proselytism in these terms: “I believe what I have got is a gift and a desire to share.” That’s why I love the Sri Lankan theologian D.T. Niles’ definition of evangelism as “one beggar telling another beggar where to find bread.”

Dr. Jules Gomes (Sep 29, 2026)

I’m not going to rag on you for thinking that way, but I do want to offer another perspective.

I’m half Mexican and half Japanese. I grew up in the United States, became a citizen, served in the Army, deployed four times, and I consider myself American without hesitation.

If the United States and Mexico were somehow at war, my loyalty would be to the United States. That does not mean I suddenly stop having Mexican roots, family traditions, food, music, language, or cultural influences.

That is the part I think gets lost when people say, “If you want to be American, then just be American.”

Being American has never required everyone to become culturally identical. Italian-Americans did not stop being Italian. Irish-Americans did not stop being Irish. Japanese-Americans did not stop being Japanese. Over time, those cultures became part of the larger American culture.

That is what assimilation actually looks like in practice: you adopt the country, its laws, its civic identity and its loyalties, while parts of the culture you came from become part of the American version of you.

A mariachi band playing The Star-Spangled Banner is a pretty good example of that. They are not rejecting America by using Mexican instrumentation. They are literally using their heritage to honor America.

So I understand the concern about national cohesion. I just think there is a major difference between refusing to integrate into a country and integrating while still remembering where you came from.

Americanization does not have to mean cultural erasure. It can mean cultural addition.

text:
Lavrentiy Beria (1899-1953), the long-serving head of Soviet security and secret police under Joseph Stalin. According to historical accounts, Beria was arrested in June 1953—shortly after Stalin's death—following a coup orchestrated by fellow high-ranking Soviet officials including Nikita Khrushchev and supported by military leaders like Marshal Georgy Zhukov. He was later tried and executed in December 1953...

Six armed generals stepped into the Kremlin conference room with their pistols drawn. Sitting at the long mahogany table, Lavrentiy Beria froze, watching his Politburo colleagues stare back in icy silence. For fifteen years, the bespectacled Georgian had served as Joseph Stalin’s chief executioner, directing the torture chambers of the Lubyanka, managing the vast slave-labor empire of the Gulag, and building the Soviet atomic bomb. Following Stalin’s death in March 1953, Beria appeared completely untouchable, commanding hundreds of thousands of security troops and holding blackmail files on every leader in the room. But in a sudden ambush organized by the men who had spent years trembling in his presence, the supreme master of Soviet terror discovered what it felt like when the state came for him.

In the vacuum following Stalin’s death, power in Moscow fractured into an uneasy collective leadership. While Georgy Malenkov assumed the premiership and Nikita Khrushchev led the party, Beria seized the Ministry of Internal Affairs, fusing the police and state security into an almighty intelligence monolith. To the astonishment of his rivals, Beria moved rapidly to pose as a reformer, halting the fabricated Doctors' Plot, releasing over a million prisoners from the Gulag, and curbing police powers. Yet his fellow ministers saw nothing benevolent in these maneuvers. They knew Beria held wiretaps on their apartments, files documenting their complicity in the purges, and private armed units across Moscow. Convinced that his liberal gestures were merely a cover to seize absolute power, his colleagues realized they had to strike before his secret police struck them.

Nikita Khrushchev organized the conspiracy with frantic secrecy. Whispering in soundproofed rooms and isolated dachas, Khrushchev quietly recruited Malenkov, Foreign Minister Vyacheslav Molotov, and defense chief Nikolai Bulganin. But neutralizing Beria presented a lethal obstacle: the Kremlin guards and security divisions ringing Moscow were all loyal to Beria’s ministry. To break the police grip, the plotters turned to the army. Khrushchev recruited Marshal Georgy Zhukov, the celebrated war hero whom Stalin had sidelined, along with trusted combat commanders. The officers loathed the secret police, whose fabricated dossiers had decimated the Red Army high command in 1937. On the morning of June 26, 1953, the generals smuggled pistols into the Kremlin beneath overcoats, waiting in an anteroom while Malenkov opened a routine cabinet meeting.

The trap snapped shut midway through the session. When Malenkov gave a prearranged nod, Khrushchev launched into a savage denunciation, accusing Beria of criminal intrigue and treason. Stunned, Beria protested, but his colleagues joined the assault, denouncing the man they had toasted days earlier. Seeing the attack mount, Malenkov pressed a buzzer beneath his desk. The double doors flew open, and Marshal Zhukov entered with General Kirill Moskalenko and four armed officers. Zhukov stepped behind the police chief and commanded: "Hands up!" Beria reached for his briefcase, but Moskalenko pinned his arms while the generals drew their weapons. Glancing in panic at Malenkov, Beria stammered, "Georgy, what is this?" Malenkov offered no answer, looking down at his desk.

text:
Saint Wenceslas by Monsignor Joseph Hanush.
.
A thousand years ago, Saint Wenceslas, Ruler of the Czechs was martyred for the Christian Faith by his brother, Bolesla, at Stara Boleslav near Prague.
.
Saint Wenceslas, born “Svaty Vaclav,” is a pacific hero. He remains the center of religious cult and national life in Czechy (Bohemia), venerated by his own people and by faithful Catholics around the world.
.
According to a patriotic legend, an army with King Wenceslas at its head is sleeping under Mount Blanik and it will arise to deliver the country during times of great national danger.
.
Research by the distinguished historian, Professor Pekar, translations from the German by the Reverend Father Striz, the work “Svati Vaclav” by Monsignor Stejskal, as well as exhaustive studies by Doctor Podlaha provide abundant material for the life of Saint Wenceslas.
.
The earliest documentary legend concerning Wenceslas dates from the first half of the tenth century. It was discovered by the Russian, Vostokoff, in 1830. It is written in Old Slav with Glagolite letters. Another legend, dating from the tenth century, was recently found by Professor Nikolsky. The Saint’s earliest biography was written in Latin. It begins, “Crescente Ficle Christiana,” and is probably of Bavarian origin. It was used by Bishop Gombold of Mantua when compiling another biography at the wish of Emperor Otto II.
.
Manuscripts from the fourteenth and fifteenth centuries can be found in the libraries of Prague and in the Convent of Boeddecke in Westphalia, contain the legend (edited by the Jesuit Father Balbin in the seventeenth century and by Father Suysken in the eighteenth century) for the Acta Sanctorum. Father Athanasius’s version in 1767, Joseph Emler’s version in 1873, and Doctor Pekar’s Latin version of 1906 (translated by Professor Truhler and Father Striz in 1921) give us the authentic narrative as first written by the monk, Christian, at the injunction of his nephew Saint Adalbert, Bishop of Prague. This monk, living at the close of the tenth century, was able to investigate and control the various accounts and reports relating to Wenceslas. Therefore, Christian’s document may be taken as historically accurate, purged of exaggeration and fancy, and containing authentic facts. It clears the memory of Drahomira, mother of Saint Wenceslas, to whose influence, as in so many parallel cases, tradition ascribed the acts committed by the evil men around her. Drahomira was a Christian, and, if she did not effectively oppose the pagan element at Court, did penance for her shortcomings to the end of her life. The document also proves the existence of the Slav Rite in Bohemia a hundred and fifty years after its introduction by Saint Cyril and Saint Methodius.
.
While the monk, Christian, was writing regarding Saint Wenceslas in Bohemia, another Czech monk, Vavrinets (Lorenzo), was doing the same at Monte Cassino, and a third treated the subject in rhythmic Latin beginning, “Oportet nos fratres . .
.
A legend from the thirteenth century, “Oriente jam sole….” acclaims Saint Wenceslas as deliverer of the Czechs from the German yoke. A script, “Vita Saint Wenceslai ut annuntietur,” commemorates the virtues of the saint and the miracles he wrought. Emperor Charles IV, the “Father of his Country,” also wrote the biography of Saint Wenceslas. A series of works on Saint Wenceslas in several languages testifies to general interest in the martyr.
.
Life of Saint Wenceslas (907 – 929)
.
Saint Wenceslas was born in 907, probably at Stochow, a village still extant near Prague. His father, Vratislav, a younger son of Prince Borivoj of the House of Premmyslides, governed a portion of the land during the reign of his elder brother, Sphytihnev. Upon the death of Sphytihnev in 915, Vratislav ascended the throne. The Saint’s mother, Drahomira, was the daughter of a Prince of the Lutici, a Slav tribe then inhabiting the country of Brandenburg, which was afterwards Germanized. Wenceslas was baptized in the Slav Rite by Father Paul, a disciple of Saint Methodius and chaplain of Princess Ludmila, grandmother of the infant. Princess Ludmila was a woman of great learning and sanctity, was one of the earliest Czech saints to be canonized, and remains a beloved figure in the history of the nation. Together with Father Paul, Ludmila superintended the education of young Wenceslas who was an apt and eager pupil. He was taught the psalms, the liturgy, and the elements of what knowledge is necessary to a future ruler, who is bound to defend as well as govern his people. At Budec College, Wenceslas acquired Latin, the cultural language of the time, and became as proficient as any aspirant to Holy Orders. He was also fully instructed in the science of warfare and the manipulation of arms, being destined, like all the princes of his time, to direct in practice as well as in theory whatever military measures were undertaken to protect his country.
.
The death of his father, Vratislav, who was killed in battle by the Magyars, interrupted the lad’s studies, for he was called to succeed. Since he was still a minor, his mother, Drahomira, acted as regent and guardian of her seven children. Drahomira is represented as jealous of Princess Ludmila’s ascendancy over Wenceslas. Drahomira lent an ear to the courtiers who asserted that Wenceslas was being trained for a monastic life rather than for a throne. Drahomira has been accused of conniving at, or even instigating, the wicked plans of her semi-Christianized courtiers, two of whom compassed the death of the venerable Princess Ludmila at her castle in Tetin in 921. At that time, the pagan element prevailed so strongly at the Court of Drahomira, even after the banishment of the two murderers, that Wenceslas could receive priests and other friends only in secret and at night.
.
On attaining his majority, the young sovereign boldly grasped the reins of government, and issued a proclamation that he would observe divine laws and punish murder severely, but still endeavor to be clement and just in all things. Drahomira, at first banished to Budec, was soon recalled to Prague by her son and we hear no more of the criminal disposition with which she had been charged, no doubt by interested calumniators intent on shifting blame from themselves. Wenceslas transferred the remains of his grandmother, Ludmila, to Saint George’s Church in the capital where they received public veneration.
.
The young Sovereign practiced Christian virtue to a degree that has identified his name with charity, beneficence, and justice. He was particularly attentive to the trials of criminals, tempered punishments, showed special mercy to the poor, and enforced better treatment of prisoners. His generosity was boundless. With his own hands, he gathered fuel in the royal forests and conveyed it to indigent homes. He ransomed the slaves captured in war and had them instructed and baptized. Wenceslas was an example in assiduity at Divine Worship and prepared, with his own hands, the bread and wine for the Holy Sacrifice. He built numerous churches, recalled the banished clergy, and took every possible means to spread Christian civilization and religious truth.
.
However, good Prince Wenceslas did not neglect the duty of maintaining the integrity of his fatherland. He had an efficient, well-clad, well-armed, and thoroughly disciplined army. Nevertheless, he was careful not to expose rashly the lives of his men. When a marauding tribe entered his territory, Wenceslas challenged its Chief, Rastislas, to settle the matter by single combat and thus avoid wanton effusion of blood. Rastislas agreed, sallied forth to meet his opponent, and dropped his weapons at the sight of a luminous cross above the head of the saint and of an angel on each side. Wenceslas did not misuse his triumph. He ceded a large tract of land and a castle to Rastislas for the duration of his life, on condition that these should ultimately revert to the Crown of Bohemia, thus furthering the consolidation and unity of the Kingdom. Another proof of his political sagacity was his treaty with the German ruler, Henry, who marched on Prague with such forces that Wenceslas could not hope to defeat them. Wenceslas offered negotiation instead of warfare and consented to pay tribute in money and cattle as well as to recognize the suzerainty of the German Monarch.
.
Thus, Wenceslas averted his country’s subjugation and the horrors of devastation and massacre in a hopeless struggle. The land of the Czechs was recognized as an entity, instead of being annexed and absorbed by its powerful neighbor. Other Slav groups in Northern Europe, whose chiefs had less perspicacity, wore themselves out in ceaseless strife against their Teuton adversaries and were eventually blotted out. Relations between Henry of Germany and Wenceslas were cordial and often marked by deference of the former to the latter. On one occasion at a reunion of Bavarian and other princes that was presided over by the German Monarch, Wenceslas was late. King Henry exclaimed angrily that no doubt the delay was due to the long prayers of the Czech and suggested that nobody should greet him when he appeared. At the moment of his entrance, however, Henry was the first to advance and embrace him, declaring that Wenceslas brought the grace of God amongst them.
.
After laboring successfully to develop the economic resources of his people and promote their spiritual welfare in every way, Wenceslas bethought himself of retiring to Rome and embracing a monastic life. However, before renouncing the throne in favor of his brother, Boleslas, he wished to see the completion of the Cathedral of Saint Vitus. He had initiated its construction to house worthily a relic of Saint Vitus that had been presented to him by King Henry upon the occasion of the treaty mentioned above, when hostilities between Czechs and Germans were averted. Unfortunately, Wenceslas was not destined to see his wish fulfilled. The dedication of the Cathedral took place after his martyrdom.
.
Prince Boleslas had not enjoyed the benefits of an upbringing under the auspices of the saintly grandmother, Princess Ludmila. He had been left to the care of semi-pagan courtiers and he easily acquired their mode of thought and rough ways. He and the rough courtiers resented the strict rules of conduct enforced by Wenceslas who was, moreover, too mild and virtuous to suit their idea of the strong ruler required by Bohemia. Prince Boleslas had, for his share of inheritance, a tract of land beyond the River Elbe, and he built himself a fine castle at the confluence of that river with the Jisera. It is said that he commanded the chief men of the district to make him a stone residence after the Roman fashion. However, they, having an abundance of timber at hand, proceeded to erect a wooden palace in the usual style, whereupon he beheaded some and reduced the others to obedience.
.
Prince Boleslas, the very opposite of Wenceslas, gathered round him a crowd of malcontents to whom the acts of Wenceslas were a constant reproach, for these men scorned to repress their passions or modify their evil lives. A plot was hatched to remove Wenceslas and replace him by his more accommodating brother who was unlikely to put a restraint on morals or to hinder freebooting expeditions. Boleslas agreed to usurp his brother’s place, conniving even at the planned murder. Realizing it would be impossible to seize Wenceslas in the strongly-fortified royal residence at Prague, Boleslas went in person to invite Wenceslas to his castle at Stara Boleslav for the patronal feast of the church. On 27 September in the year of 929, on the Feast of Saints Cosmas and Damian, Wenceslas assisted at the celebrations in Stara Boleslav and remained after Mass, at his brother’s request, to witness the games and contests arranged in honor of the day. The conspirators had intended to assassinate him as he sat at the banquet but, when they looked on his tranquil countenance, their courage failed. As Wenceslas left the hall, two of his retainers approached him and warned him that something was afoot. They had a saddled horse in readiness and urged him to make his escape. However, Wenceslas refused and returned instead to the banqueting hall and resumed his seat. He lifted his glass and called on the company to toast, “Saint Michael, whom we pray to guide us to peace and eternal joy.” Not all of those present answered, “Amen,” but Wenceslas withdrew undisturbed and recited the psalms as usual before laying down to rest. Meantime, the conspirators conferred at the house of Hnevys and summoned Boleslas to assist. It was resolved that Wenceslas should be slain on his way to early morning Mass. Boleslas gave orders to the priests of the Saints Cosmas and Damian Church that the church doors should be barred at that hour. The church was connected with Boleslas ‘s castle by a private passage where it was deemed the crime could be safely committed.
.
At the sound of the Mass bell, Wenceslas rose and went towards the church along the passage where Boleslas awaited him. The other conspirators were hidden in an adjoining courtyard.
.
Wenceslas greeted Boleslas and again thanked him for his hospitality. In response the traitor exclaimed, “Yesterday I did my best to serve you worthily, but this must be my service today!” He drew a sword from beneath his cloak and struck at the head of Wenceslas, who parried the blow, snatched the weapon from his assailant, and threw him on the ground.
.
Wenceslas might have dispatched Boleslas and remained master of the situation, for the other conspirators rushed forward only when Boleslas’ s cries for help showed that he was alive, although worsted in combat. However, Wenceslas was no fratricide, even in self- defense, and preferred to succumb rather than kill Boleslas. Cesta, Tyra, and Hnevys dashed to the rescue of Boleslas and stabbed Wenceslas ruthlessly, with one blade-thrust piercing his side. He fell at the church door murmuring, “May God forgive you this, my Brother!”
.
The date of Saint Wenceslas’ martyrdom is September 28th, 929. When the assassins had accomplished their foul deed, they escaped and Drahomira was apprised of her eldest son’s tragic fate. Stricken with grief, she hastened to convey the body, covered with wounds, inside the church, whose outside walls were bespattered with blood. The red stains remained visible for centuries.
.
A legend says that on that ill-starred night, a son was bom to Boleslas and named “Strach-Hvas” (Dread Feast) by the people – in allusion to the perfidious banquet given in honor of Prince Wenceslas before he was murdered.
.
Boleslas took care that the funeral of his brother was carried out with due royal pomp. Father Paul, the former tutor of Wenceslas, had the mournful task of officiating at the burial. The martyr was interred close to the church that was subsequently enlarged to include the grave within its precincts. Drahomira and her devoted daughter, Pribyslava, fearing they too might be victims of Boleslas’s partisans, had fled before the funeral took place. Her suspicions were fully justified by the violent deaths that followed of Wenceslas’s servants and friends, which included many priests.
.
Sometime after the martyrdom, Wenceslas appeared to his sister, Pribyslava, and told her where to find (near the church door) his ear, which had been slashed off by a sword cut. She discovered it exactly in the spot indicated and had Wenceslas’ coffin opened to place the severed ear near his head. When the body was later transferred to Prague, say the chroniclers, the ear was found adhering to its proper place as firmly as if it had never been detached.
.
Boleslas, tormented by remorse, sought to make reparation and to ease his conscience by transporting Wenceslas’ mortal remains to the capital. He gave orders that this should be done at early dawn, on March 4th, 932, under pain of death for those charged with the task if they delayed in its performance. However, the river Rokytnice was in flood, and therefore impassable. The convoy fell on their knees and implored Saint Wenceslas to help them. They then went the nearest forest to seek wood for a raft, leaving the coffin on the bank. Upon their return, they saw it on the other side. After fording the stream on horseback, they found the coffin dry and unharmed as if miraculously transported without touching the water. Another obstacle confronted them at the river Vltava where the bridge was broken down. Again, they had recourse to Saint Wenceslas, and suddenly the coffin became so light that they easily waded with it on their shoulders to the opposite bank. A third incident confirmed their trust in the power of the saint. Some distance from the Castle of Prague, the horses drawing the bier suddenly stopped and a team of twelve oxen was requisitioned to replace the horses. The animals strained ineffectually until the arrival of the archpriest of the Church of Our Lady accompanied by his clergy.
.
It was now broad daylight and a great crowd had assembled to join in the archpriest’s invocation for Divine assistance. At the close of the prayer, a single team of oxen (all the others having been unyoked) moved forward of their own accord and never paused in the steep ascent until they reached the new Church of Saint Vitus, Wenceslas’s own foundation. Here the martyred Prince was interred amidst touching manifestations of love and grief by his devoted people.
.
The Cult of Saint Wenceslas
.
Saint Wenceslas was a martyr for the Faith that he had upheld against pagan opposition.
.
Wenceslas displayed many qualities throughout his life, qualities that prove his sanctity and justify the title of Saint given him by the Czech people. Some of these include:
.
His zeal for erecting churches that are among the most beautiful in the world;
.
His maintenance of priests to regularly celebrate the Divine Liturgy and teach their flocks not only religious doctrine, but also every useful branch of knowledge;
.
His rectitude in forbidding condemnation of accused persons without full proof of their guilt;
.
His generosity and charity in protecting the humble against their masters;
.
His refusal to participate in the pagan feasts and rites that were prevalent at that time in Bohemia;
.
His exemplary life that caused his soldiers and subjects to see in him as a monk rather than a prince.
.
We have no exact date of his canonization, which was in all probability pronounced by Bishop Detmar or by his successor, Bishop Adalbert, of Prague.
.
In those days, the process of canonization was not reserved exclusively to the Papacy, as it has been since the reign of Pope Alexander III. Yet, we have incontestable proofs that he was duly canonized, for a Sacramentary of the time of King Otto, crowned in 985, mentions September 28th, in the ecclesiastical calendar, as the Feast of Saint Wenceslas, Martyr.
.
The concourse of pilgrims to his tomb became so immense that Prince Spytinev constructed a new church with three naves to make room for them. Among the earliest cures carried out at the shrine of Saint Wenceslas were those of a leprous woman and a paralytic from France – both were instantaneous and complete. The Czech people soon attributed a wider scope to the power of Wenceslas, a scope beyond that of healing bodily ills. As fervent lover of his people, Wenceslas was besought in all national crises. The Chronicler Cosmo relates that in 1002, when the Poles invaded Bohemia, Saint Wenceslas protected the land and secured the return of the rightful ruler Oldrich. The victory of Domazlice, gained in 1040 by Bratislas I over the Germans, and another victory in 1126, when Prince Sobeslas defeated the forces of King Lothar, were attributed to the intercession of Saint Wenceslas. In 1260, the army of King Premysl-Ottokar II of Bohemia was encamped near the village of Kessenbrun at the confluence of the Morava and the Danube. They were surrounded on three sides by the army of Beta II, King of Hungary. The Czechs called on God and Saint Wenceslas, then marched boldly to the attack and routed the enemy.
.
On the feast of his patron and namesake, King Wenceslas II won a great battle at Sieradce on the Wartha in 1292. On the other hand, we find that it was generally held that no hostilities should be entered upon, if possible, on that day, and truces were often arranged between conflicting parties so the feast could be worthily celebrated.
.
Relics
.
Soon after his martyrdom, relics of Saint Wenceslas were laid on the altars of several churches. Bishop Hildibald deposited a piece of linen saturated with Saint Wenceslas’ blood in the Saint Lawrence Chapel of Hilberstadt Cathedral in the year 992. Relics of Saint Adalbert and Saint Wenceslas were placed in the High Altar of Eucharia’s Church at Trier in 1148. Pieces of his garments were also kept in the churches of Tegernsee, Bamberg, Salzburg, Rhinegan, and Quedlimburg where an altar was consecrated in honor of Saints Remy and Wenceslas. In Bohemia, there are numerous relics of Saint Wenceslas, the Bohemian national saint. The Czech Bishop Daniel deposited them, in the presence of King Vladislav and Queen Judith in the churches of Bohnice, Recany, Cirkvice, and in Saint James’s Church of Prague.
.
Churches
.
A great number of churches were founded in honor of Saint Wenceslas, notably one at Prosek, near Prague, in 972, and another near the Castle itself of Prague, which was destroyed by Joseph II of Austria in 1782. One of the oldest extant is that of Saint Wenceslas at Stara Boleslav. Prince Svatopluk of Moravia built a church at Olomouc in honor of Saint Wenceslas, and Robert, Bishop of Cracow, consecrated another in that city in the year 1142. In the fifteenth century, two Kings of Bohemia, Ladislas Posthumus and Wenceslas II, appointed priests to say Mass regularly at the altar of Saint Wenceslas in Aix-la-Chapelle. Hundreds of churches dedicated to the national Saint of the Czechs are to be found in various cities of Central Europe and at least four can be found in the United States of America. The basilica of Saint Peter in Rome has a Saint Wenceslas altar erected by Bishop Berka of Olomouc, who died at Rome in 1333. This altar was later dedicated to Saint Erasmus; but Pope Urban VIII ordered that an altar should be dedicated to Saint Wenceslas in the new basilica. This was done in 1628 and his relics were solemnly transferred at that time. The altar is in the right nave (where the Vatican Council of 1870 was held) and bears the inscription, “Altar of Saint Wenceslas, Duke of Bohemia, offered by Hynec, Bishop of Olomouc.”
.
It was richly endowed for the celebration of Masses and the Office of the Dead.
.
The Czech people revere Saint Wenceslas as their particular patron and he is honored by the entire Slavic race. On September 28th, in 1092, King Bratislas II assisted at a splendid church celebration of the Feast of Saint Wenceslas and entertained courtiers and nobles with extraordinary magnificence over three days. On this date, national assemblies were usually convoked, churches were consecrated, and important enterprises were begun.
.
The Office of Saint Wenceslas was introduced in the Roman Breviary in the thirteenth century. The story of Saint Wenceslas, as it now stands in the second Noctum, dates from the fourteenth century.
.
When Pope Urban VIII extended the Feasts of Kings Hermengildus and Stephen to the universal Church, Archbishop Matthew Ferdinand Zubeck of Prague obtained the same privilege for the Feast of the Bohemian Prince and Saint Benedict XIII made the Feast obligatory. The Mass and Office had previously been inserted in Missal and Breviary under Pro aliquibus locis.
.
A touching expression of the Czech people’s love for Saint Wenceslas is the ancient canticle “Svaty Vaclav,” sung today with as much fervor as in the Middle Ages. The author of the first four verses was probably Bishop Bechyne, who composed them at the time of the Brandenburg invasion in 1272. Yet, the Jesuit historian, Father Balbi, ascribes them to Bishop Ernest of Pardubice in the fourteenth century. The Calixtine Hussites themselves chanted “Svaty Vaclav,” and bore his image on their shields with the chalice above the banner and the first four lines of the canticle below. One of these shields is preserved in the National Museum at Prague and another in the Hermitage at Petrograd. The canticle has always had a national as well as a religious character. In the rebellion of 1848, against Hapsburg absolutism, the help of Saint Wenceslas was invoked to repel and overcome Germanization...

text:
Looking at Sultan Suleyman's tomb, he composes this poem:

A million elite troops once marched on Hungary and Austria; 
golden banners and jade-adorned maidens flanked his mighty army. 
His awesome might once shook all of Europe;
now his bones lie buried beneath these steps. 
Golden lamps light the night like a dream of Mount Li;
heavy curtains hang in the dusk over this quiet hall.
Walking the path of accompanying graves at this mausoleum, 
flowers offered by a young girl, I am overcome with feeling.

当日威棱震欧土，只今骸骨葬阶壝。
金灯照夜骊山梦，緫帐垂昏阁殿清。
循省昭陵从葬路，赠花幼女不胜情。)

Several Washington state colleges and universities offer cannabis-related courses, certificates, and research programs, mostly as continuing education or professional training rather than full degree majors. https://t.co/I1q8MQe7gm 
Washington legalized recreational cannabis in 2012, and the industry has driven demand for trained workers in cultivation, retail, product development, compliance, and medical consulting. Institutions have responded with targeted programs, often in partnership with providers like Green Flower or the Academy of Cannabis Science.
Community colleges
•  Seattle Central College runs the Cannabis Institute in partnership with the Academy of Cannabis Science. It offers a Medical Cannabis Consultant certificate approved by the Washington State Department of Health—the first such program in the state. Courses cover science-based training for retail staff, medical professionals, and others; they are available online. https://t.co/7ftdgUiwKL 
•  Tacoma Community College (continuing education) offers multiple online certificate programs, including Cannabis Cultivation Specialist, Cannabis Retail & Sales Specialist, Cannabis Product Development Specialist, Medical Cannabis Specialist, Cannabis Compliance Specialist, and a shorter Cannabis Associate Certificate. These are typically 8–16 weeks and partner with Green Flower. https://t.co/TDReRyycut 
Four-year universities
•  Gonzaga University (Center for Lifelong Learning) provides certificate programs in Cannabis Health Care & Medicine and Cannabis Compliance & Risk Management, also in partnership with Green Flower. These are aimed at career changers and industry professionals. https://t.co/k1uuJqWwHe 
•  Western Washington University offers non-credit Green Flower cannabis courses. https://t.co/nK6WMIeUW9 
•  Washington State University operates a Cannabis Research Center that supports faculty and student research on health, policy, agriculture, and related topics. It also issues guidance on allowable teaching and research activities given federal restrictions. https://t.co/xP13XUsSeQ 
•  University of Washington has a Center for Cannabis Research and related programs (including through the Addictions, Drug & Alcohol Institute) that fund research, webinars, and education on public health and policy aspects. Some specific course topics, such as medicinal cannabis and chronic pain, have been offered. https://t.co/hdWhJOGW74 
These programs are generally certificates or short courses rather than bachelor’s or associate degrees in “cannabis studies.” They focus on practical industry skills, medical consulting requirements, or academic research. Availability, costs, and start dates change, so check the individual college websites for current offerings.

text:
🚨 OKLAHOMA TAXPAYERS’ DATA WAS BREACHED. MONTHS LATER, WE STILL DON’T KNOW HOW BIG IT WAS.

If there is one place you really don’t want a cybersecurity problem, it’s the system holding your tax information.

But that’s what happened with Oklahoma’s Taxpayer Access Point, OkTAP.

The Oklahoma Tax Commission discovered unauthorized access to tax information on December 19, 2025.

The information involved was classified as personally identifiable information and tax information.

That’s significant.

OkTAP handles extremely sensitive information, including names, Social Security numbers and tax records. Businesses also use the system to submit W-2 and 1099 information.

The state says affected individuals were notified by mail and offered 12 months of complimentary credit monitoring and fraud assistance.

But questions remain.

The state’s public cybersecurity disclosure wasn’t posted until April 7, 2026, months after the unauthorized access was discovered.

And the state’s own notice says it remains unclear how many people were affected.

So nearly ten months later:

🔴 How many taxpayers were affected?

🔴 Exactly what information was accessed?

🔴 Were Social Security numbers exposed, and for how many people?

🔴 Were W-2 or 1099 records accessed?

🔴 When were taxpayers notified?

🔴 How did someone gain access to OkTAP, and for how long?

🔴 What has been changed to prevent it from happening again?

The state has confirmed unauthorized access involving personally identifiable and tax information. But the public information still doesn’t tell us exactly which records were accessed.

And that’s the problem.

We shouldn’t have to guess.

Taxpayers are required to provide extraordinarily sensitive information to the government.

When the system protecting that information is breached, Oklahomans deserve to know what happened, how extensive it was, what was exposed and how quickly taxpayers were warned.

Because when tax information and potentially Social Security numbers are involved, “we don’t know how many people were affected” is a pretty important unanswered question.

text:
'NO NEED FOR URGENCY': ONE FED LINE LIFTED STOCKS INTO THE FINAL HOUR. THE 30-YEAR BOND BARELY BUDGED:

At 3:26pm ET the S&P 500 is at 7,675.14, -8.55 / -0.11%, with about half an hour of regular trading left. At its worst it was at 7,653.55, -30.14 / -0.39%, and it sat on that floor until 2pm. The Nasdaq-100 is at 30,355.59, +78.78 / +0.26%. The Dow Jones Industrial Average is at 51,362.19, -119.32 / -0.23%. Smaller companies still trail, with the iShares Russell 2000 ETF (IWM) at $278.83, -$1.19 / -0.42% today.

The verdict going into the bell: one sentence from a Federal Reserve official broke the afternoon standoff in stocks' favor. It moved the bond that tracks the Fed's next few meetings. It barely touched the bond that tracks the next few decades, and that one is still the ceiling. A green finish needs 8.55 more points.

At 2pm, New York Fed President John Williams, vice chair of the Fed committee that sets interest rates, released remarks for an audience at the University at Buffalo. The line that mattered: "With the policy action we took at our September meeting, there is no need for urgency." The Fed raised its rate on September 16, to 3.75%-4.00%, and Williams still expects more: "one further upward adjustment of the federal funds target range may be appropriate late this year." Reuters read the remarks as pushing back on bets for an increase at the next meeting, October 27-28. His outlook: inflation near 3.5% at the end of 2026 and back to the Fed's 2% goal by 2028; growth of 2.25% this year; unemployment at 4% next year.

Stocks answered inside a minute. The S&P 500 was at 7,655.98 when the remarks posted and touched 7,666.58 before 2:01. By 2:41pm it reached 7,682.33, just 1.36 points short of Monday's 7,683.69 close.

The bond market split in two:
- 2-year Treasury yield, the one most tied to where traders expect the Fed to take rates: 4.939% at 1:57pm, 4.885% at 2:06pm. Now 4.891%, -3.3 basis points (hundredths of a percentage point) on the day.
- 10-year, the rate mortgages and business loans are priced from: 5.285% just before 2pm, 5.255% now, still +1.3 on the day.
- 30-year: 5.610% before the remarks, 5.599% two minutes after, 5.592% now, +3.0 on the day. It touched 5.621% early this afternoon, a level CNBC put at the highest since 2002.

A Fed president speaks for the next few meetings. The 30-year is what investors charge to lend to Washington for three decades, so it prices inflation and government borrowing far past any meeting Williams will attend. It is up today even with U.S. crude (WTI) at $89.29 a barrel, -$3.31 / -3.57% since Monday's settlement, near its low of the day. Cheaper oil usually cools inflation worries and pulls long-term yields down with it. Not today. Since the 2:41 high, the 30-year has held near 5.59% and the S&P 500 has drifted back.

Underneath, chips lead: VanEck Semiconductor ETF (SMH) at $607.83, +$7.82 / +1.30% today. Utilities, among the heaviest borrowers in the market, are second: Utilities Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLU) at $39.72, +$0.47 / +1.18% today. At the bottom, energy producers are following crude, with the Energy Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLE) at $61.49, -$0.61 / -0.98% today, next to the Materials Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLB) at $49.00, -$0.47 / -0.95% today, and the Consumer Staples Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLP) at $81.77, -$0.52 / -0.63% today. The Nasdaq-100 holds plenty of chipmakers and few oil, chemical or grocery-aisle companies, which is how it is green while the S&P 500 is red.

The one heavyweight going hard the other way is Apple (AAPL) at $330.52, -$7.88 / -2.33% today, the worst of the eight biggest U.S. tech stocks and about $115B of market value gone since Monday's close. Apple is on none of the six Len5 watchlists: at about 39 times its last year of profit and 4.3% under its September 22 high of $345.34, it lacks the discount the value-minded Len5es wait for.

What would count as a strong or a weak close:
- Strong: the S&P 500 above 7,683.69, Monday's close. That turns a day that was down 0.39% at its worst into a gain, and says the Williams relief outlasted the long bond.
- Weak: back under 7,653.55, the floor it touched five separate times between 11:20am and 2pm. That erases the whole Williams bounce.
- In between, a small loss near here: the relief held but could not finish the job.
- The tell alongside it: the 10-year back above 5.285%, where it stood before the remarks, would mean the bounce has lost its reason. A 2-year still under 4.90% says the relief is sticking.

What can still move it before 4pm:
- No more U.S. economic reports are scheduled today.
- In the final ten minutes, the exchanges publish the buy and sell orders waiting to trade at the closing price. A lopsided pile can push the last print several points for reasons unrelated to news. The bigger quarter-end rebalancing wave waits for Wednesday's close.
- Washington's formal answer to Iran's plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Iran's foreign minister, Abbas Araghchi, says he expects it today through Qatari mediators. No set time. A flat no is the headline most able to lift crude off its low.

Then the first real test of "no urgency" arrives Wednesday at 8:30am ET: the Bureau of Economic Analysis's August PCE price index, the Fed's preferred inflation gauge. Core prices, leaving out food and energy, are forecast +3.4% from a year earlier vs 3.3% in July, and +0.3% for the month vs +0.2%. Friday at 8:30am ET brings the Bureau of Labor Statistics' September jobs report.

Williams bought stocks an afternoon by putting the Fed's next move on a slower clock. The 30-year never took the offer, and in less than 18 hours the August inflation report gets to rule on which of them read the economy right.

Not investment advice.

text:
DAILY WALKING WITH GOD
Octavius Winslow
29 09 26 – P.M.

"For if the blood of bulls and of goats, and the ashes of an heifer sprinkling the unclean, sanctifies to the purifying of the flesh: how much more shall the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered himself without spot to God, purge your conscience from dead works to serve the living God?" Hebrews 9:13, 14

But for a crucified Savior, there could be no possible return to God; in no other way could He, consistently with the holiness and rectitude of the Divine government, with what He owes to Himself as a just and holy God, receive a poor, wandering, returning sinner. Mere repentance and humiliation for and confession of sin could entitle the soul to no act of pardon. The obedience and death of the Lord Jesus laid the foundation and opened the way for the exercise of this great and sovereign act of grace. The cross of Jesus displays the most awful exhibition of God's hatred of sin, and at the same time the most august manifestation of His readiness to pardon it. Pardon, full and free, is written out in every drop of blood that is seen, is proclaimed in every groan that is heard, and shines in the very prodigy of mercy that closes the solemn scene upon the cross. Oh blessed door of return, open and never shut to the wanderer from God! how glorious, how free, how accessible! Here the sinful, the vile, the guilty, the unworthy, the poor, the penniless may come. Here, too, the weary spirit may bring its burden, the broken spirit its sorrow, the guilty spirit its sin, the backsliding spirit its wandering. All are welcome here. The death of Jesus was the opening and the emptying of the full heart of God; it was the outgushing of that ocean of infinite mercy that heaved, and panted, and longed for an outlet; it was God showing how He could love a poor guilty sinner. What more could He have done than this? what stronger proof, what richer gift, what costlier boon could He have given in attestation of that love? Now, it is the simple belief of this that brings the tide of joy down into the soul; it is faith's view of this that dissolves the adamant, rends asunder the flinty rock, smites down the pyramid of self-righteousness, lays the rebellious will in the dust, and enfolds the repenting, believing soul in the very arms of free, rich, and sovereign love. Here, too, the believer is led to trace the sin of his backsliding in its darkest lines, and to mourn over it with his bitterest tears—

"Then beneath the cross adoring,
Sin does like itself appear;
When the wounds of Christ exploring,
I can read my pardon there."

If the Lord has restored your soul, dear reader, remember why He has done it—to make you hate your sins. He hates them, and He will make you to hate them too; and this He does by pardoning them, by sprinkling the atoning blood upon the conscience, and by restoring unto you the joys of His salvation. And never is sin so sincerely hated, never is it so deeply deplored, so bitterly mourned over, and so utterly forsaken, as when He speaks to the heart, and says, "Your sins are forgiven you, go in peace." As though He did say, "I have blotted out your transgressions, I have healed your backslidings, I have restored your soul; that you may remember and be confounded, and never open your mouth any more because of your shame, when I am pacified toward you for all that you have done, says the Lord God."

If your heavenly Father has restored your soul, not only has He done it from the spring of His own unchangeable love, but that which has prevailed with Him was the power of the sweet incense of the Redeemer's blood before the mercy-seat. Moment by moment does this fragrant cloud go up, bearing as it ascends all the circumstances of all the Israel of God. There is not only the blood already sprinkled on the mercy-seat, which has satisfied Divine justice, but there is the constant pleading of the blood, by Jesus, the Priest, before the throne. Oh precious thought, oh comforting, encouraging truth, for a soul retreading its steps back to God! Of its own it has nothing to plead but its folly, its ingratitude, its wretchedness, and its sin; but faith can lay its trembling hand upon this blessed truth—faith can observe Jesus clothed in His priestly garments, standing between the soul and God, spreading forth His hands, and pleading on behalf of the returning believer the merits of His own precious obedience and death. And thus encouraged, he may draw near and touch the scepter: "If any man sin, we have an Advocate with the Father, Jesus Christ the righteous." "Christ is not entered into the holy places made with hands, which are the figures of the true; but into heaven itself, now to appear in the presence of God for us.

a lawsuit would be likely if Ralph Norman received the most votes as a write-in.South Carolina’s “sore-loser” statute (S.C. Code § 7-11-210) requires primary candidates to pledge they will not “offer or campaign as a write-in candidate” after losing. The Republican Party chairman can seek a court injunction to stop any such campaigning. Norman has already publicly disavowed a write-in effort and pledged to support Darline Graham.

The losing campaign or the state Republican Party would almost certainly file an election contest or seek to block certification. No modern South Carolina precedent exists for throwing out a write-in plurality on these grounds, so the outcome would be uncertain and would likely be decided after the election"

text:
LOL! Your AI on the fritz? 

There's pressure to apply the "equal time" mandate on The View. IF enforced, The View would be shut down if it didn't comply.

EXCERP:
Consider: FCC Chairman Brendan Carr’s stated reason is enforcement of the federal equal-time rule (Section 315 of the Communications Act). That rule generally requires a broadcast station that gives airtime to one legally qualified candidate to offer comparable time and placement to opposing candidates, if requested.

There is a longstanding exemption for “bona fide news interview” programs. Carr’s position is that The View has not shown it still qualifies for that exemption. His public comments and the FCC’s actions focus on these points:

Triggering event: Democratic Texas Senate candidate James Talarico appeared on the show in February 2026. The FCC opened an inquiry into ABC’s Houston station over that appearance.⁠AP News
January 2026 guidance: The FCC said it had not been presented with evidence that the interview portions of current daytime or late-night talk shows qualify for the bona fide news exemption, and that programs motivated by “partisan purposes” rather than newsworthiness do not qualify.⁠AP News
Carr’s own statements: He has said The View is “asserting” it is bona fide news like Meet the Press, but “there’s obviously questions” about that given its guest lineup and format. He earlier called an investigation “worthwhile.” He has described the goal as holding broadcasters accountable so they cannot “decide what we can say, what we can think, who we can vote for.”⁠The Independent
ABC’s counter is that the FCC already treated The View as a bona fide news interview program in a 2002 ruling, that the show is produced by the network’s news division, and that the current probe is unprecedented and chills speech. Critics, including the Democratic FCC commissioner, have called the inquiry government intimidation aimed at a show that is often critical of President Trump. Carr rejects that characterization and says the rule simply requires comparable time, not that any particular guest must appear on The View itself.⁠Politico

In short: Carr frames the action as applying an old statute more strictly to talk shows he views as partisan rather than news; opponents frame it as selective pressure on a program the administration dislikes. The dispute is now in a formal FCC proceeding over whether The View still gets the news-interview exemption.

text:
When talking to potential acquirers, founders benefit from clarity on the process and timeline.

Here are the 5 most common questions:

1. Who are you, and what do you buy?

Helium Ventures acquires, owns, and operates venture backed companies that were not able to hit escape velocity. Priyank and I started it in 2025. We built Stilt (YC W16) and sold it to JG Wentworth in 2022. We focus primarily on digital software companies with mostly US customers (or based in the US), up to $10M in revenue, in any vertical. We don't buy hardware, e-commerce, or crypto companies for now.

We also buy assets and companies where team is getting acquihired, but the founders would like to continue to serve the customers. We take over tech, customer success, ops, sales, and product with our team and steward the company.

We also buy second products - if one product is growing faster and you want to sell the legacy product with complicated IP/legal/contract/etc complexity.

2. How do you value my company?

We are product and innovation buyers. So it's ok if you are burning money and have not been profitable or if it took you time to find the idea maze. We look at what the business can sustainably earn and work back from there. We understand the chaos of startup We also want to be confident that we can steward the company and serve your customers well. We buy all cash, cash-free and debt-free (which means we don't take your cash in the bank or take on liabilities).

3. How fast can you close, and will you actually close?

We don't have an investment committee. Priyank and I make all the decisions, and you work with us directly. We don't waste time on things like QoE, projections, or pro forma. We look at the numbers and the code ourselves. We don't need months of diligence to give you an offer. We ask for simple things that are readily available, eg 12 months of bank statements, your contracts, and team roster

You will get a verbal offer, then a term sheet (if you agree), then docs and diligence in parallel. Our fastest close was 2 weeks. Most take about a month. Once we sign an LOI, we have never retraded or walked away.

4. What happens to my customers, team, and product?

We run it. We step in as CEO and CTO, answer support tickets ourselves, and our engineers are in the codebase within a week. We are not spreadsheet buyers. We work hard on product and GTM. We use your advice and guidance to build the next phase of the company. Our best company grew revenue 50% in 6 months after we took over.

5. Do I have to stay? Is there an earnout?

It's your call. Most founders go heavy for 2-3 months, then advise a few hours a week. We usually offer non-contingent payouts, incentivize founders over 6-12 months, and don't tie it to performance. We pay what we promised. And more importantly, we don't have non-competes.

If you're a founder with real revenue stuck in the wrong cap table, we'd love to chat.
